title: The Natufian villages
text: Hunter-gatherers in the Levant settle in round stone houses and harvest wild grain with flint sickles.

title: The first murder
text: Caine kills Abel in the fields, is cursed, and goes into the wilderness east of Eden.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Hunters in the karst caves
text: Late Ice Age hunters shelter in the caves of the Moravian Karst and follow reindeer and horse across the plain.

title: The Ice Age ends
text: The cold snap called the Younger Dryas breaks; forests spread north and the great herds thin.

title: Jericho's first settlers
text: People settle by the spring at Jericho, one of the oldest continuously lived-in places.

title: The pillars of Gobekli Tepe
text: Hunters raise carved stone pillars on a hill in Anatolia, a sacred place built before farming.

title: The carved beasts on the hill
text: The foxes, vultures and boars carved at Gobekli Tepe are read by Garou lorekeepers as a caern raised in honour of the Fera.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Caine meets Lilith
text: In the wilderness Caine finds Lilith, who teaches the first powers of the blood and is later betrayed.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Farming begins
text: Wheat, barley and lentils are first sown on purpose in the hills of the Fertile Crescent.

title: The Impergium begins
text: As farming begins, the Garou start to cull the growing human herds; the Impergium lasts about three thousand years (W20 pdf 71).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

title: Goats tamed
text: Herders in the Zagros keep the first tame goats.

title: Cattle and sheep tamed
text: Wild aurochs and mouflon are bred into cattle and sheep in Anatolia and the upper Euphrates.

title: The wall and tower of Jericho
text: Jericho's people build a stone wall and round tower, among the first public works anywhere.

title: The First City
text: Caine founds Enoch and Embraces the Second Generation; mortals and the childer live under one ruler.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Rice farming
text: Rice is first farmed along the middle Yangtze in China.

title: Squash and gourds in the Americas
text: People in the Americas begin to grow squash and gourds.

title: Catalhoyuk
text: A town of mud-brick houses entered through the roofs grows on the Konya plain, home to several thousand.

title: The houses of bulls
text: Some Noddists claim the bull horns and vulture paintings of Catalhoyuk mark a town that fed the First City.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Farmers reach Europe
text: Farming families cross from Anatolia into Greece and the Balkans.

title: Mehrgarh
text: A farming village rises at Mehrgarh below the Bolan Pass, ancestor of the Indus cities.

title: The bone flutes of Jiahu
text: Villagers at Jiahu in China play flutes of crane bone and scratch signs on tortoise shell.

title: Doggerland drowns
text: The rising sea covers the low land between Britain and the continent.

title: The cold event
text: A sudden cooling lasting two centuries strains the first farms of Europe and the Near East.

title: The Concord
text: Sixteen tribes meet and agree to end the Impergium, nearly nine thousand years before the modern nights (W20 pdf 40-41, 71).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

title: The first canals
text: Farmers in southern Mesopotamia dig canals from the rivers to water their fields.

title: The Flood
text: A great flood destroys Enoch; the Second Generation die or vanish, and their childer rule the ruins.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Lepenski Vir
text: Fishers by the Danube's Iron Gates carve river-stone heads with fish faces.

title: The Black Sea rises
text: Some scholars hold that the Black Sea filled quickly from the Mediterranean about now, drowning its shore villages.

title: The first farmers in Moravia
text: Linear Pottery farmers settle the loess plains of southern Moravia in long timber houses.

title: The forest and the plough
text: The first fields cut into the Moravian woods; Garou of the region mark where the farmers may go and where they may not.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Talheim grave
text: At Talheim in Germany a whole farming community is killed and buried in one pit.

title: The Second City
text: The Third Generation raise a new city after the Flood, each ruling a quarter with their own childer.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

title: Eridu
text: Eridu, held by later Sumerians to be the first city of kings, builds its first temple to the water god Enki.

title: The Yangshao villages
text: Painted-pottery villages spread along the Yellow River.

title: Maize
text: Farmers in Mexico breed maize from the wild grass teosinte.

title: The roundels
text: Farmers of central Europe build great round ditched enclosures, some of them in Moravia, perhaps for gatherings and rites.

title: The first megaliths
text: Stone tombs and standing stones rise in Brittany.

title: The gold of Varna
text: A grave at Varna on the Black Sea holds the oldest worked gold yet found.

title: Stones the fae remember
text: The tales of the Kithain place the Mythic Age in the time when the long stone rows of Carnac were raised.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Copper worked
text: Smiths in the Balkans smelt copper; the Copper Age begins.

title: The quarrels of the Third Generation
text: The rulers of the Second City feud over power and their childer, and the city's peace frays.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

title: The Ubaid traders
text: Ubaid culture spreads from southern Mesopotamia up the rivers and along the Gulf.

title: The wheel
text: The first wheels turn in Mesopotamia and on the steppe.

title: Horses tamed
text: Steppe people north of the Black Sea begin to keep and ride horses.

title: The fall of the Second City
text: The Second City falls to war and the childer's revolt; the Antediluvians scatter across the world.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

title: The War of Rage begins
text: After the Impergium the Fera rise against the Garou, and the Garou turn on the changing breeds; many lines are hunted near to their end (Tribebook Silent Striders pdf 16).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Antediluvians scatter
text: After the Second City, the Third Generation go their ways: some to the mountains, some to the rivers, some into the sea of mortal peoples.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The hill folk of the Alps
text: Herders cross the high passes of the Alps with copper axes and flint.

title: Uruk grows
text: Uruk becomes the largest city in the world, with tens of thousands living inside its walls.

title: The temples of Malta
text: Islanders on Malta build great stone temples.

title: The potter's wheel and the plough
text: Sumerians use the fast potter's wheel and the ox-drawn plough.

title: Naqada
text: The towns of Upper Egypt grow rich under chiefs buried with painted pots.

title: Osiris rules
text: In the legend of the Reborn, Osiris rules the Two Lands as a god-king, with Isis beside the throne.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The striders by the river
text: The Silent Striders keep their oldest home among the shrines of the Nile.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Corded Ware ancestors
text: Herders from the steppe begin to push west into central Europe.

title: The iceman
text: A man is shot with an arrow and dies on a pass in the Alps; the ice keeps the body for five thousand years.

title: Writing
text: Scribes at Uruk press signs into clay tablets to keep the temple's accounts, the start of writing.

title: Hieroglyphs
text: The first hieroglyphs are written in Upper Egypt.

title: Set murders Osiris
text: Set kills Osiris and scatters the body across Egypt, and takes the throne.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Spell of Life
text: Isis gathers the pieces of Osiris and, with the help of the gods, works the Spell of Life; Osiris rises.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Sutekh in the Two Lands
text: The Followers of Set tell that their founder walked among the first kings of Egypt and was worshipped as a god.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Narmer unites Egypt
text: The king of Upper Egypt takes the Delta; the Narmer Palette shows the first king of a single Egypt.

title: Horus against Set
text: Horus, son of Osiris and Isis, wars with Set for the throne of Egypt.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Skara Brae
text: Farmers on Orkney build the stone village of Skara Brae, with stone beds and dressers.

title: Stonehenge's first ditch
text: A circular bank and ditch is dug on Salisbury Plain; the stones come later.

title: The Sumerian city-states
text: Ur, Uruk, Lagash, Kish and Nippur grow into rival city-states, each with its own god.

title: The first Shemsu-heru
text: Osiris shares the Spell of Life with chosen followers, the first of the Reborn who serve Horus.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The old gods remembered
text: In the reckoning of the Fallen, the gods the Sumerians worship are half-remembered faces of angels from before the Fall.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The early Indus towns
text: Towns of the Indus valley begin building with baked brick.

title: Monks of the high passes
text: The Akashic Brotherhood counts its oldest roots among hermits in the mountains above the Indus.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The flood layer at Shuruppak
text: A deep layer of river silt at Shuruppak marks a great flood, the kind later remembered in the flood stories.

title: Corded Ware in Moravia
text: Herders who bury their dead with corded beakers and stone battle-axes settle across Moravia.

title: The Longshan towns
text: Walled towns of black polished pottery rise along the Yellow River.

title: Gilgamesh of Uruk
text: Gilgamesh, later the hero of the oldest written epic, rules Uruk about now.

title: The Old Kingdom
text: Egypt's Old Kingdom begins, the age of the great pyramids.

title: Djoser's step pyramid
text: Imhotep builds the step pyramid for King Djoser at Saqqara, the first great stone building.

title: Imhotep the builder
text: Later Hermetic masters honour Imhotep as a founder of the arts of building, healing and writing.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The royal graves of Ur
text: The kings and queens of Ur are buried with gold, lyres and dozens of attendants.

title: Harappa and Mohenjo-daro
text: The great Indus cities lay out straight streets, drains and granaries.

title: The Great Pyramid
text: The Great Pyramid of Khufu is finished at Giza, the tallest building on earth for nearly four thousand years.

title: Tombs that the Reborn know
text: The Shemsu-heru know the pyramid fields as places where the walls between the living and the dead are thin.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Great Sphinx
text: The Sphinx is carved from the bedrock at Giza.

title: The sarsens of Stonehenge
text: The great sarsen circle and the trilithons are raised at Stonehenge.

title: The stone ring caern
text: The Fianna sing that the stone circles of Britain were raised over caerns, and that the rings still answer the moon.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Bell Beaker folk
text: Bell Beaker pottery and copper daggers spread from Iberia to Britain and central Europe.

title: The Sacred Peace of Lagash
text: Garou and Fera keep a truce at Lagash in Sumer for a time, before the War of Rage returns.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Stele of the Vultures
text: Eannatum of Lagash defeats Umma and sets up a stone showing vultures over the dead.

title: Urukagina's reforms
text: Urukagina of Lagash curbs the greed of priests and officials, the first known law reform.

title: The archives of Ebla
text: Thousands of clay tablets at Ebla in Syria record a trading city's business.

title: Sargon of Akkad
text: Sargon founds the Akkadian empire, the first to rule all Mesopotamia.

title: A Methuselah behind the throne
text: Some Ventrue claim that their line advised the first kings of Akkad; the Brujah call it a boast.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Enheduanna's hymns
text: Sargon's daughter Enheduanna, high priestess at Ur, writes hymns to Inanna, the first author known by name.

title: Unetice bronze
text: The Unetice culture works bronze in Bohemia and Moravia and trades tin and amber across central Europe.

title: Pepi II's long reign
text: Pepi II rules Egypt for perhaps ninety years; the Old Kingdom weakens.

title: The great drought
text: A drought lasting decades strikes from Egypt to the Indus; Akkad collapses.

title: The First Intermediate Period
text: The Old Kingdom breaks apart into rival provinces after low Nile floods.

title: The Gutians
text: Mountain raiders called the Gutians overrun Akkad.

title: The Third Dynasty of Ur
text: Ur-Nammu rebuilds Sumer, raises the great ziggurat of Ur and issues a law code.

title: The laws of Ur-Nammu
text: The oldest surviving law code sets fines in silver for injuries.

title: The Xia
text: Chinese tradition places the first dynasty, the Xia, and the flood-tamer Yu the Great about now.

title: Yu and the waters
text: The Kuei-jin say the first dynasty was founded when the dragons of the rivers were bargained with, not beaten.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Middle Kingdom
text: Mentuhotep II reunites Egypt from Thebes.

title: The palaces of Crete
text: The Minoans build the first palaces at Knossos and Phaistos.

title: The bull and the labyrinth
text: Garou tales of the War of Rage place a hidden lair of the changing breeds under the palace hills of Crete.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The chariot
text: Chariots with spoked wheels appear on the steppe east of the Urals.

title: Greek speakers in Greece
text: Peoples speaking an early Greek settle the Greek mainland.

title: Assyrian traders in Anatolia
text: Merchants from Assur keep a trading colony at Kanesh in Anatolia, sending tin and cloth.

title: The Indus cities decline
text: The great Indus cities shrink as rivers shift and trade fails.

title: The Wessex graves
text: Chiefs on the chalk downs of Wessex are buried with gold and amber.

title: Babylon's first dynasty
text: An Amorite dynasty takes Babylon, then a small town.

title: The first Baali
text: The Baali tell that their first sire drew power from things older than Caine in the swamps of southern Mesopotamia.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Egyptian mathematics
text: Egyptian scribes copy problems of fractions and areas, later gathered in the Rhind papyrus.

title: The Setites in ancient Egypt
text: The Followers of Set grow strong in the cult centres of the Delta, as the Encyclopaedia records.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Hammurabi becomes king
text: Hammurabi takes the throne of Babylon and spends thirty years making it an empire.

title: The code of Hammurabi
text: Hammurabi has his laws carved on a basalt stele: an eye for an eye, set by rank.

title: Bronze hoards
text: Bronze axes, rings and ingots are buried in hoards across Moravia, as offerings or savings.

title: Hoards the dead guard
text: Wraiths of the Unetice dead are said to linger over the hoards buried with their names.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Nebra sky disc
text: A bronze disc inlaid with gold sun, moon and stars is buried on a hill in Germany.

title: The Hyksos
text: Foreign kings called the Hyksos rule the Nile Delta, bringing the horse and chariot to Egypt.

title: Set worshipped at Avaris
text: The Hyksos kings honour Set at Avaris; the Followers of Set count this a high time of their cult.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Thera erupts
text: The volcano of Thera blows apart, burying the town of Akrotiri in ash and sending waves across the Aegean.

title: A dream drowned
text: Kithain tales speak of a shining island of the Mythic Age lost to fire and sea; scholars point to Thera.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Shang
text: The Shang dynasty rules the Yellow River plain from walled capitals.

title: The shaft graves of Mycenae
text: Mycenae's kings are buried with gold masks.

title: The Hittites sack Babylon
text: The Hittite king Mursili I raids down the Euphrates and sacks Babylon.

title: The New Kingdom
text: Ahmose I drives out the Hyksos; Egypt's New Kingdom begins.

title: The Reborn and the expulsion
text: The Shemsu-heru are said to have fought beside Ahmose's army against the Followers of Set in the Delta.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Vedic peoples
text: Peoples speaking an Indo-Aryan tongue settle north India; the hymns of the Rigveda take shape.

title: The Valley of the Kings
text: Egypt's kings begin to be buried in hidden tombs in the Valley of the Kings.

title: The Tumulus culture
text: Central Europeans bury their dead under earth mounds, the barrows of the Bronze Age.

title: Barrows on the ridges
text: Bronze Age barrows crown the ridges of Moravia; the Garou of the land take some for caerns and leave others well alone.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Hatshepsut rules
text: Hatshepsut takes the throne of Egypt as king and rules for about twenty years.

title: The voyage to Punt
text: Hatshepsut's ships sail down the Red Sea to Punt and bring back incense trees and ebony.

title: Megiddo
text: Thutmose III defeats a league of Canaanite kings at Megiddo, the first battle recorded in detail.

title: Mycenaeans at Knossos
text: Mycenaean Greeks take over the palace of Knossos and its Linear B scribes.

title: The minotaur's court
text: Some Cainite legends place an elder of the beast-blooded clans in the halls under Knossos.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Mitanni
text: The kingdom of Mitanni rules northern Mesopotamia with chariot lords.

title: The Amarna age of letters
text: Kings of Egypt, Babylon, Mitanni and the Hittites write to each other as brothers and trade gold for horses.

title: Akhenaten's new faith
text: Akhenaten puts the sun disc Aten above all other gods and builds a new capital at Amarna.

title: The Aten heresy
text: The Reborn remember Akhenaten's reign, which the books put at 1364 to 1347 BCE, as a time when the old rites of the dead were shut away and the Shemsu-heru hid.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Nefertiti's bust
text: The sculptor Thutmose carves the painted bust of Queen Nefertiti.

title: Tutankhamun restores the gods
text: The boy king Tutankhamun abandons Amarna and restores the old gods.

title: Tutankhamun buried
text: Tutankhamun dies young and is buried with a small but rich tomb that robbers miss.

title: The Urnfield culture
text: Central Europeans begin to burn their dead and bury the ashes in urns in large cemeteries.

title: Urnfield hillforts
text: Hillforts ringed with earth and timber are built on the heights of Moravia.

title: The urnfields
text: Burning the dead changes nothing for the wraiths of Moravia's urnfields, who gather in the shadow of the cemeteries.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Ramesses II
text: Ramesses II begins a reign of sixty-six years and carves his temples at Abu Simbel.

title: Kadesh
text: Egyptians and Hittites fight the largest chariot battle known at Kadesh; both claim victory.

title: The first peace treaty
text: Ramesses II and the Hittite king Hattusili III sign a peace treaty, copies of which survive in both tongues.

title: Troy VII burns
text: The citadel of Troy is sacked about now, the event that may lie behind the Iliad.

title: The Tollense battle
text: Thousands fight at a river crossing in northern Germany, the oldest large battle known in Europe.

title: Israel in Canaan
text: A people called Israel is first named in Canaan, on a stone of Pharaoh Merneptah in 1208.

title: Prophets and judges
text: In later hunter lore the judges and prophets of Israel are the first mortals remembered for standing against the night's creatures by faith alone.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Hittite empire falls
text: Hattusa is abandoned and burned; the Hittite empire breaks up.

title: The Olmec
text: The Olmec build their first ceremonial centre at San Lorenzo and carve colossal stone heads.

title: The First Comers
text: The Pure Ones tell that their tribes held the lands across the ocean long before the Garou of Europe came, with their own peace among the breeds.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: The Shadow Lords in the Americas

title: Ramesses III fights the Sea Peoples
text: Ramesses III turns back the Sea Peoples in a battle on the Nile Delta, carved on the walls of Medinet Habu.

title: The Bronze Age collapse
text: Ugarit, Mycenae, Pylos and many other cities fall to raiders, drought and quakes; trade and writing vanish across the region.

title: Elders go to ground
text: The fall of the Bronze Age cities sends old Cainites into long sleep; some claim the collapse was a war among them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Elam takes Babylon's gods
text: The Elamites sack Babylon and carry off the Code of Hammurabi and the statue of Marduk.

title: The Greek dark age
text: Greece loses its palaces and writing; people live in small villages for three centuries.

title: The Phoenician cities
text: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos rise as sea-trading cities.

title: Iron spreads
text: Iron tools and weapons spread through the Levant and Anatolia.

title: The Third Intermediate Period
text: Egypt splits between the priest-kings of Thebes and kings in the Delta.

title: The Zhou overthrow the Shang
text: King Wu of Zhou defeats the last Shang king at Muye; the Zhou claim the Mandate of Heaven.

title: The Mandate of Heaven
text: The Kuei-jin date their weakness to sunlight from the Chou, and tell that the Japanese spirit Mikaboshi advised the new dynasty (KotE pdf 12).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: David in Jerusalem
text: David makes Jerusalem the capital of Israel.

title: The Phoenician alphabet
text: The Phoenicians write with an alphabet of 22 letters, the ancestor of Greek and Latin writing.

title: The later Vedas
text: The Vedic hymns are gathered and the kingdoms of the Ganges plain grow.

title: Fires on the plateau
text: The first fire-priests of the Iranian plateau tend their altars, later honoured as a root of the Celestial Chorus and the Ahl-i-Batin.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Late Urnfield hillforts
text: Hillforts multiply in central Europe as chiefs compete.

title: The Tuatha and the Fomorians
text: Kithain legend sets the great war of the Tuatha against the Fomorians in this age, long before the Sundering.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Solomon's temple
text: Solomon builds the first temple in Jerusalem.

title: The seal of Solomon
text: Fallen and Earthbound alike tell stories of the king who bound spirits with a ring and a name.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Himalayan War begins
text: Akashic and Euthanatos masters begin a war in the mountains that runs, by one count, to 300 BCE (M20 pdf 123; Sorcerers Crusade pdf 68).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Libyan pharaohs
text: Shoshenq I, of Libyan descent, takes Egypt's throne and raids Judah.

title: The kingdom divides
text: After Solomon the kingdom splits into Israel in the north and Judah in the south.

title: The kingdom of Kush
text: Kushite kings at Napata on the upper Nile build their own kingdom.

title: Chavin de Huantar
text: The temple centre of Chavin draws pilgrims in the high Andes.

title: The Villanovan villages
text: Iron-using villages of central Italy grow into the Etruscan cities.

title: Ashurnasirpal II
text: Ashurnasirpal II makes Assyria the terror of the Near East and builds a palace at Nimrud.

title: The great feast at Nimrud
text: Ashurnasirpal feeds nearly seventy thousand guests for ten days to open his capital.

title: Qarqar
text: Shalmaneser III fights a league of kings including Ahab of Israel at Qarqar.

title: The salt mines of Hallstatt
text: Miners dig salt deep into the mountain at Hallstatt in the Alps, giving the Iron Age culture its name.

title: The Gonghe regency
text: Nobles drive out King Li of Zhou; from 841 Chinese history has a year-by-year record.

title: Carthage founded
text: Phoenicians from Tyre found Carthage, in legend led by the princess Elissa, called Dido.

title: A new city by the sea
text: The Brujah tell that their elders came to Carthage soon after its founding and saw in it the chance of a city where Cainite and mortal could live side by side.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Sammu-ramat
text: Queen Sammu-ramat, later the legendary Semiramis, rules Assyria for her young son.

title: The Fall
text: In the reckoning of the Fallen, the angels who loved humanity rebel against Heaven at the dawn of the human race and are cast down.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Age of Wrath
text: The Fallen walk the young world openly and war with the loyal hosts; humans worship and fear them.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Fallen cast into the Abyss
text: The rebel angels are locked away in the Abyss; a few escape the binding as the Earthbound.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The first dead
text: The dead of the first villages linger in the Shadowlands, with no city or ferryman to guide them.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The laws of the First City
text: Caine forbids the Second Generation to make more childer; the command is broken.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Third Generation made
text: The Second Generation Embrace the thirteen who will be remembered as the Antediluvians.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The childer slay their sires
text: In some tellings the Third Generation kill their own sires after the Flood; in others the Second simply vanish.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Triat
text: Garou lorekeepers tell that the Wyld, the Weaver and the Wyrm once kept the balance, before the Weaver went mad and bound the Wyrm.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

title: Magic open to all
text: Mages remember the Mythic Age as a time before consensus, when gods and spirits answered common people.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Dreaming and waking as one
text: In Kithain legend the fae live beside mortals, and the Dreaming touches every field.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The first August Personages
text: The Kuei-jin speak of the oldest age, when the courts of Heaven and the Yomi kept the Great Cycle turning.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Ratkin under the cities
text: The Ratkin say they were made to keep the human herds small, and took to the first cities when the Impergium ended.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: Ratkin Plagues of Asia and Europe

title: The Siberian War
text: The Encyclopaedia records a War of Rage fought across Siberia.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Saraam and the Cat Kings
text: The Bastet keep courts among the city kings of Sumer, as their tales hold.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Saulot the wise
text: Saulot, founder of the Salubri, studies in the Second City and travels east to seek the end of the Beast.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

title: Troile and the city
text: The Brujah say their founder Troile prized the Second City above all and fought its fall.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

links.title: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

title: The Tzimisce go north
text: The founder of the Tzimisce leaves the ruins for the mountains to the north, toward the Carpathians.
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Nosferatu's curse

text: The Encyclopaedia's tale of a breed ordained by both sun and moon.

title: Krapina and Ananasa's Web
text: An old lair at Krapina tied to the spider queen, as the Encyclopaedia records.

title: Hemudu
text: Villagers at Hemudu near the Yangtze mouth build timber houses on stilts and grow rice.

title: The Venus of Hluboke Masovky
text: Farmers of southern Moravia make clay figurines of women for their homes and shrines.

title: The Carnac rows
text: Thousands of standing stones are set in rows at Carnac.

title: The Sahara dries
text: The green Sahara turns to desert; herders move toward the Nile and the south.

title: The copper axe in Moravia
text: Copper tools reach Moravian farmers through trade from the Balkans.

title: The passage tombs of Ireland
text: Farmers in Ireland raise passage tombs in the Boyne valley.

title: Newgrange
text: The passage tomb at Newgrange is built so the midwinter sunrise lights its inner chamber.

title: The hollow hills
text: Kithain call the Boyne tombs the first hollow hills, doors of the sidhe long before the Sundering.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Proto-Elamite writing
text: Scribes at Susa write in their own signs.

title: The first dynasty tombs
text: The early kings of Egypt are buried at Abydos with their servants.

title: Kish and the first kings
text: The Sumerian king list names Kish as the first city to hold kingship after the flood.

title: The fall of Liangzhu
text: The jade-working city of Liangzhu near the Yangtze mouth is abandoned, perhaps after floods.

title: Caral
text: The city of Caral in the Peruvian desert raises platform mounds, the oldest city of the Americas.

title: The Ness of Brodgar
text: The great stone halls of the Ness of Brodgar stand between two stone rings on Orkney.

title: The Pyramid Texts
text: Spells for the dead king's rise to the stars are carved inside the pyramid of Unas.

title: The spells on the walls
text: The Reborn read the Pyramid Texts as a clumsy echo of the true Spell of Life.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Indus ships at Ur
text: Indus traders sail to Sumer with carnelian beads; Sumerians call the land Meluhha.

title: Shimao
text: A great stone-walled town rises on the loess at Shimao in northern China.

title: Shulgi
text: King Shulgi of Ur sets up a road network with rest houses and standard weights.

title: Amber from the north
text: Baltic amber passes through Moravia toward the south.

title: The palace of Mari
text: The palace archive of King Zimri-Lim at Mari records spies, prophets and diplomacy.

title: The prophets of Mari
text: Mari's letters record ecstatic prophets who carry messages from the gods to the king.

title: Crete's palaces rebuilt
text: Earthquakes wreck the Cretan palaces; they are rebuilt grander than before.

title: Oracle bones
text: Shang diviners crack ox bones and turtle shells with heat and write the questions on them, China's oldest writing.

title: The ancestors answer
text: The Kuei-jin say the Shang kings spoke with true ancestors through the cracks, and the spirits answered.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Book of the Dead
text: Egyptians begin to bury spells for the afterlife on papyrus, later called the Book of the Dead.

title: Ugarit's alphabet
text: Scribes at Ugarit write an alphabet in cuneiform signs.

title: Assyria rises
text: Ashur-uballit I makes Assyria a great power.

title: Lady Fu Hao
text: The Shang queen and general Fu Hao leads armies and is buried with hundreds of bronzes.

title: The Epic of Gilgamesh
text: The standard version of the Epic of Gilgamesh is written down.

title: The Rigveda completed
text: The hymns of the Rigveda reach their final form, though still learned by heart.

title: The tomb robbery trials
text: Tomb robbers in the Valley of the Kings are tried and confess.

title: Tiglath-Pileser I
text: Tiglath-Pileser I campaigns to the Mediterranean and hunts lions and wild bulls.

title: The Philistines
text: The Philistine cities of the coast fight Israel's tribes.

title: The urnfields at Klentnice
text: Large urnfield cemeteries spread across southern Moravia below the Palava hills.

title: The incense road
text: Camels carry frankincense and myrrh from south Arabia north to the Levant.

title: Saba
text: The kingdom of Saba grows rich on incense in south Arabia.

title: Geometric pottery
text: Greek potters paint vases with bands of zigzags and meanders.

title: Urartu
text: The kingdom of Urartu rises around Lake Van.

title: Iron reaches Moravia
text: The first iron tools reach Moravia; the Hallstatt age begins there.

title: Tyre's queen flees
text: Elissa of Tyre flees a brother king and sails west, in the tale that ends with Carthage.

title: Jomon pottery
text: Hunter-gatherers in Japan make some of the world's oldest pottery.

title: Hunters across the Americas
text: Hunters with fluted spear points have spread through both Americas.

title: The rock paintings of the Sahara
text: Herders paint cattle, giraffes and dancers on the rocks of a green Sahara.

title: The last hunters of Moravia
text: Bands of hunters and fishers still live by the rivers of Moravia before the farmers come.

title: Lengyel villages
text: Farmers of the Lengyel culture build fortified villages in southern Moravia.

title: The Baden villages
text: The Baden culture's villages spread through Moravia, with wheeled carts and copper.

title: The Moravian cave burials
text: People of the Copper Age bury some of their dead in the caves of the Moravian Karst.

title: Bell Beakers in Moravia
text: Bell Beaker people settle in Moravia beside the Corded Ware herders.

title: Unetice graves
text: The Unetice dead are buried crouched on their sides with bronze pins and rings.

title: Fortified Bronze Age towns
text: Bronze Age settlements in Moravia gain ditches and palisades.

title: Bronze hoards of the Urnfield age
text: Moravian smiths bury hoards of sickles, axes and scrap bronze.

title: The hillfort at Hostyn
text: An Urnfield hillfort stands on Hostyn hill, a height later held sacred.

title: The hill of Hostyn
text: The Garou of Moravia keep a caern on the wooded height of Hostyn, and the hillfort's builders leave offerings there.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The antler masks of Star Carr
text: Hunters by a lake in Yorkshire wear red-deer antler headdresses, perhaps for rites.

title: The statues of Ain Ghazal
text: Villagers near Amman shape tall plaster figures with staring eyes.

title: The plastered skulls
text: The people of Jericho keep their dead's skulls, rebuilt in plaster with shell eyes.

title: Skulls kept at home
text: Wraith lore holds that the plastered skulls of Jericho were Fetters, keeping the first dead close to the living.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The long houses and their dead
text: The Linear Pottery farmers of Moravia bury their dead beside the villages, crouched with pots and adzes.

title: Vinca signs
text: Potters of the Vinca culture scratch signs on clay that some take for an early script.

title: The temples of Eridu grow
text: Each rebuilding raises Eridu's temple higher, toward the later ziggurat.

title: Horses milked and ridden
text: The Botai people of the Kazakh steppe keep herds of horses.

title: The kurgans
text: Steppe herders bury their chiefs under earth mounds called kurgans.

title: The first Gangrel run with the herds
text: The Gangrel tell that their founder ran with the horse peoples of the steppe, far from any city.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Warka vase
text: A carved alabaster vase from Uruk shows a procession bringing offerings to Inanna.

title: The walls of Uruk
text: Uruk's walls reach nine kilometres, later credited to Gilgamesh.

title: The Egyptian calendar
text: Egypt keeps a calendar of 365 days in three seasons tied to the Nile flood.

title: The Great Bath
text: Mohenjo-daro's builders make a large waterproof brick bath, perhaps for rites.

title: Kubaba of Kish
text: The Sumerian king list names Kubaba, a tavern keeper, as the only woman to rule Kish.

title: Sintashta
text: The fortified towns of Sintashta on the steppe bury warriors with chariots.

title: Abraham's age
text: Hebrew tradition places the patriarch Abraham's journey from Ur to Canaan about now.

title: Babylonian mathematics
text: Babylonian scribes work in base sixty and know Pythagoras' rule a thousand years early.

title: Kerma
text: The Nubian city of Kerma rules the middle Nile and rivals Egypt.

title: Cyclopean walls
text: Mycenaean builders raise walls of stones so large later Greeks thought giants had moved them.

title: The Upanishads take root
text: Thinkers of the Ganges plain begin the speculation later written in the Upanishads.

title: The fall of Pylos
text: The palace of Pylos burns, baking its clay records hard.

title: The oracle at Dodona
text: Hermetic historians trace the first Greek oracles to the oak of Dodona, older than Delphi.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Book of Changes
text: The Zhou begin the divination system later written down as the Yijing.

title: Zarathustra's age
text: Many scholars place the prophet Zarathustra between 1500 and 1000 BCE on the steppe.

title: Zarathustra and the first Adversary
text: The Encyclopaedia's account of Zarathustra and the first Adversary belongs here.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Assyrian siege craft
text: Assyrian armies bring battering rams and siege towers to the walls of their enemies.

title: Aram-Damascus
text: The Aramean kingdom of Damascus fights both Israel and Assyria.

title: The Mesha stele
text: King Mesha of Moab sets up a stone telling of his war with Israel.

title: Baal the Destroyer is beaten
text: The Baali begin in the Second City; their leader leads them against it and is beaten back (V20 pdf 402).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Troile Embraced

links.title: The fall of the Second City in the Book of Nod

title: Mashkan-shapir abandoned
text: The Babylonian city of Mashkan-shapir is emptied, perhaps after a change in the river.

title: Nergal goes to Ashur
text: In Baali lore their city of Mashkan-shapir falls and the elder Nergal moves to Ashur (Clanbook Baali pdf 23-24).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Kindred crowd into Egypt
text: As more Cainites come to Egypt, Set's rule of the land weakens (Mummy 1st pdf 64).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Horus drives out Set
text: Horus, with allies from the west, drives Set out of Egypt (Mummy 1st pdf 65).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Ainu of the north
text: The Ainu people's ancestors live in the northern islands of Japan.

title: The Ainu and the spirits
text: Kindred of the East places the Ainu in the islands by this age, with their own bond to the spirits (Kindred of the Thousand Hells pdf 44).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Time of Babel
text: After the Time of Atrocities and the Long March, the war of Heaven and the Fallen calms into the Time of Babel (Houses of the Fallen pdf 19, 73).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Lilith cast out
text: In the lore of Ur and Babylon, Lilith is the first woman, Adam's equal, and is cast out of Eden into the unformed world (Revelations of the Dark Mother pdf 4).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: Caine weds Zillah
text: Bound to a crone by her blood, Caine in turn gives Zillah his blood for three nights and marries her (Book of Nod pdf 12-13).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Bahari
text: Lilith's cult, the Bahari, keep her teaching; in their telling Caine's line turns on her for thirteen generations (Revelations of the Dark Mother pdf 4-5).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The Wyrm splits
text: Caught in the Weaver's web, the Wyrm goes mad and splits into Beast-of-War, Eater-of-Souls and the Defiler (W20 Book of the Wyrm pdf 12-14).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The oldest leaf of the Book of Nod
text: By the reckoning of the book's own scholar, its oldest fragment was written just before Sumer (Book of Nod pdf 19).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Reed of Thoth and the Cupbearers of Isis
text: Hatshepsut and Thutmose III call a gathering that founds two lodges of magicians (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 20).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: A hundred sects
text: Within a century the two Egyptian lodges split into more than a hundred rival sects (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 20).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The first Olympic Games
text: By Greek reckoning the first games are held at Olympia in honour of Zeus.

title: Rome founded
text: By Roman tradition Romulus founds Rome on the Palatine on 21 April.

links.title: The White Howlers' War with Rome

title: Homer
text: The Iliad and the Odyssey take shape in the Greek world about now.

title: Greeks settle in Italy
text: Greek traders found Pithekoussai on Ischia, the first Greek settlement in the west.

title: Tiglath-Pileser III
text: Assyria becomes a standing empire that moves whole peoples to break revolts.

title: Israel falls to Assyria
text: Assyria takes Samaria and carries off the northern tribes of Israel.

title: Hallstatt princes
text: Chiefs of the Hallstatt culture are buried in wagon graves with gold and Greek bronzes.

title: The Germanic tribes move south
text: The Get of Fenris tell of their kin tribes moving south into Europe about now (Tribebook Fenris pdf 21).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Sennacherib at Jerusalem
text: Sennacherib besieges Jerusalem; Hezekiah pays tribute and the city stands.

title: Sennacherib destroys Babylon
text: Sennacherib floods and razes Babylon.

title: Assyria takes Egypt
text: Esarhaddon takes Memphis and drives the Kushite pharaoh south.

title: Ashurbanipal's library
text: Ashurbanipal gathers tens of thousands of tablets at Nineveh, the Gilgamesh epic among them.

title: Jimmu's court
text: Japanese tradition dates the first emperor, Jimmu, to 660 BCE.

title: The first Yamato court
text: Kindred of the East keeps the traditional date for the first imperial court (KotE pdf 145).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The first coins
text: The kings of Lydia strike coins of electrum, the first true coinage.

title: Cyrene founded
text: Greeks from Thera found Cyrene on the Libyan coast.

title: Draco's laws
text: Draco writes down the laws of Athens, harsh enough to give their name to harshness.

title: Nineveh falls
text: Babylonians and Medes sack Nineveh; Assyria is finished within a few years.

title: Carchemish
text: Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon defeats Egypt at Carchemish.

title: Massalia founded
text: Greeks from Phocaea found Massalia, later Marseille.

title: Carthage, capital of the Phoenician world
text: By now Carthage leads the Phoenician cities of the west, and its Brujah court is the pride of the clan (Clanbook Brujah pdf 18).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Azure Dragons cross to Japan
text: Kuei-jin of the Azure Dragon follow Korean migrants to Japan (KotE pdf 145).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Solon's reforms
text: Solon cancels debts and ends debt slavery in Athens.

title: Jerusalem destroyed
text: Nebuchadnezzar destroys Jerusalem and the first temple; the people of Judah go into exile in Babylon.

title: The eclipse battle
text: An eclipse halts a battle between Lydia and the Medes; Thales of Miletus is said to have predicted it.

title: The Buddha born
text: Tradition places the birth of Siddhartha Gautama about now, though many date it later.

title: Croesus
text: Croesus of Lydia becomes a byword for wealth.

title: Confucius born
text: Kong Qiu, later called Confucius, is born in the state of Lu.

title: Cyrus the Great
text: Cyrus of Persia overthrows the Medes and founds the Persian empire.

title: The Byci skala burial
text: In a cave of the Moravian Karst a Hallstatt chief is buried with a wagon, bronzes and dozens of others, some of them killed for the rite.

title: The dead of the bull cave
text: The cave of Byci skala holds a crowd of Hallstatt wraiths bound to their lord and to the bronzes left with them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Cyrus takes Babylon
text: Babylon opens its gates to Cyrus; the exiles of Judah may go home.

title: Persia takes Egypt
text: Cambyses defeats Egypt at Pelusium.

title: Persian Egypt
text: The Reborn see Egypt pass to foreign kings for the first of many times.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Darius I
text: Darius I takes the Persian throne and orders the empire into satrapies with a royal road.

title: The Roman Republic
text: Rome drives out its last king and becomes a republic under two consuls.

links.title: The White Howlers' War with Rome

title: A republic of the dead
text: Wraith histories say the dead of Rome set up a republic of their own, the pattern for Stygia (Wraith: Renegades pdf 26-28).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: The White Howlers' War with Rome

title: Athenian democracy
text: Cleisthenes reforms Athens into a democracy of citizens.

title: The Night of Fana
text: The Ahl-i-Batin date their beginning to the Night of Fana (Sorcerers Crusade pdf 69).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Ionian revolt
text: The Greek cities of Ionia revolt against Persia.

title: The Dragon River War
text: Mages fight the Dragon River War from 496 to 480 BCE (Sorcerers Crusade pdf 69).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: The Warring States and the Silk Road

title: Marathon
text: Athenians beat the Persian landing at Marathon.

title: Thermopylae
text: Leonidas and his Spartans hold the pass at Thermopylae before they are overwhelmed.

title: Salamis
text: The Greek fleet destroys the Persian fleet in the strait of Salamis.

title: Himera
text: The Greeks of Sicily defeat a Carthaginian army at Himera.

title: Plataea
text: The Greeks end the Persian invasion at Plataea.

title: The Warring States
text: Chinese states begin two and a half centuries of war.

title: The Twelve Tables
text: Rome's laws are written on twelve bronze tablets in the Forum.

links.title: The White Howlers' War with Rome

title: La Tene
text: The La Tene style of Celtic art spreads from the upper Rhine and Danube.

title: The Parthenon
text: Athens begins the Parthenon under Pericles.

title: The Peloponnesian War
text: Athens and Sparta begin a war that lasts until 404.

title: The plague of Athens
text: Plague kills perhaps a third of Athens, Pericles with them.

title: The Brujah mourn Athens
text: The Brujah, lovers of the Greek city, watch the plague and the war break Athens.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Athens surrenders
text: Athens yields to Sparta.

title: Socrates dies
text: Athens condemns Socrates, who drinks hemlock.

title: The Gauls sack Rome
text: Gauls under Brennus defeat Rome at the Allia and sack the city.

links.title: The White Howlers' War with Rome

title: Wolves and the Gauls
text: The Fianna sing that their Kinfolk rode with the Gauls who sacked Rome.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: The White Howlers' War with Rome

title: Plato's Academy
text: Plato opens his school at the Academy.

title: Leuctra
text: Thebes breaks Spartan power at Leuctra.

title: Philip II of Macedon
text: Philip II takes the throne of Macedon and builds a new army.

title: Chaeronea
text: Philip beats Athens and Thebes; Greece falls under Macedon.

title: Alexander's accession
text: Philip is murdered and Alexander takes the throne at twenty.

title: Granicus
text: Alexander crosses into Asia and defeats the Persian satraps.

title: Issus
text: Alexander routs Darius III at Issus.

title: The siege of Tyre
text: Alexander builds a mole to the island city of Tyre and takes it after seven months.

title: Alexandria founded
text: Alexander takes Egypt and founds Alexandria.

title: The Macedonian in Egypt
text: The Reborn's own histories mark Alexander's taking of Egypt and the founding of Alexandria (Mummy 2nd pdf 24).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Gaugamela
text: Alexander destroys the Persian army at Gaugamela.

title: Persepolis burns
text: Alexander's army burns the palace at Persepolis.

title: Hydaspes
text: Alexander beats King Porus at the Hydaspes; his army refuses to go further.

title: Alexander dies
text: Alexander dies at Babylon at thirty-two; his generals divide the empire.

title: The Maurya empire
text: Chandragupta Maurya founds an empire across north India.

title: The Ptolemies
text: Ptolemy I takes the title of king of Egypt.

title: Set and the Ptolemies
text: The Reborn hold that Set corrupts the Ptolemaic kings and that Horus passes into the Underworld (Mummy 2nd pdf 24, 27).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Library of Alexandria
text: The Ptolemies found the Museum and the Library of Alexandria.

title: Masters at the Library
text: Hermetic tradition counts the scholars of Alexandria among its founders in spirit.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Euclid
text: Euclid writes the Elements of geometry at Alexandria.

title: The First Punic War
text: Rome and Carthage go to war over Sicily.

title: The Ventrue light the fuse
text: Clanbook Ventrue says the clan stirred the First Punic War by way of Syracuse (pdf 19-20).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Mylae
text: Rome's new fleet wins its first sea battle with boarding bridges.

title: Ashoka turns to the Buddha
text: After the slaughter at Kalinga the Maurya emperor Ashoka turns to Buddhism.

title: Carthage loses Sicily
text: Rome wins at the Aegates Islands and takes Sicily.

title: The First Emperor
text: Qin Shi Huang unites China and calls himself the First Emperor.

title: Fu Xia and the First Emperor
text: The Encyclopaedia places Fu Xia at the First Emperor's court.
ref: Real history; character from the Encyclopaedia entry linked, year a house reading

title: Hannibal crosses the Alps
text: Hannibal leads an army with elephants over the Alps into Italy.

title: Cannae
text: Hannibal surrounds and destroys a Roman army at Cannae.

title: The Great Wall joined
text: The First Emperor links the northern walls into one line.

title: The terracotta army
text: Qin Shi Huang is buried with thousands of clay soldiers.

title: A Lord of the Dead
text: Kindred of the East tells that Qin Shi Huang became a Lord of the Dead (KotE pdf 142-145; Dark Kingdom of Jade pdf 34-35).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Han
text: The Han dynasty takes power fifteen years after the Qin unification.

title: Zama
text: Scipio defeats Hannibal at Zama; Carthage sues for peace.

title: Cynoscephalae
text: The Roman legion beats the Macedonian phalanx.

title: The Memphis decree
text: Priests at Memphis write a decree in hieroglyphs, demotic and Greek.

title: Pydna
text: Rome ends the kingdom of Macedon.

title: The Maccabees
text: The Maccabees revolt against the Seleucid king.

title: War is declared again
text: Rome declares war on Carthage fifty years after the last; Clanbook Ventrue puts the clan behind it (pdf 19-20).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: The White Howlers' War with Rome

title: Carthage destroyed
text: Rome takes Carthage after a three-year siege, sells its people and razes the city.

title: The fall of Brujah Carthage
text: Ventrue treachery ends Brujah Carthage; Malkavians help ruin it, and the Brujah never forgive Rome (V20 pdf 58; V20 Dark Ages pdf 54).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Baali at Carthage
