text: Henry IV kneels in the snow at Canossa before Pope Gregory VII.

title: Vratislaus king
text: Vratislaus II is crowned king of Bohemia for his lifetime.

title: Cainites among the taifas
text: The Encyclopaedia places Cainites among the taifa kingdoms of Spain.
ref: Real history; character from the Encyclopaedia entry linked, year a house reading

title: The crusade preached
text: Pope Urban II calls the First Crusade.

title: Crusaders in Prague
text: Crusaders passing through Prague attack its Jews.

title: The fae swear a truce
text: About a century before the 1230 setting of Dark Ages: Fae, the fae swear the Oath-Truce, which is near its end by that year (Dark Ages: Fae pdf 8, 25, 40).
ref: Legend; the year is a house reading

title: The First Crusade takes Jerusalem
text: The crusaders take Jerusalem and kill much of its people.

title: The Weeks of Blood
text: The Encyclopaedia's Weeks of Blood follow the fall of Jerusalem.
ref: Real history; character from the Encyclopaedia entry linked, year a house reading

links.title: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

title: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
text: The Encyclopaedia places Cainites in the new crusader kingdom.
ref: Real history; character from the Encyclopaedia entry linked, year a house reading

links.title: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

title: The first gargoyles
text: The Tremere make the first gargoyles for their war with the Tzimisce (V20 Dark Ages pdf 83).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Chlumec
text: Sobeslav I of Bohemia defeats the German king Lothar at Chlumec.

title: Saulot's end
text: Tremere drinks the soul of Saulot in 1133 (V20 Dark Ages pdf 41).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Ardan of the Golden Lane
text: Ardan, of the Tremere chantry in Prague, is Embraced (House of Tremere pdf 82).
ref: Real history; character from the Encyclopaedia entry linked, year a house reading

title: The Moravian princes besiege Prague
text: The Moravian princes rise against Duke Vladislaus II and besiege Prague.

title: Edessa falls
text: Zengi takes Edessa; the Second Crusade follows.

title: Vladislaus king
text: Frederick Barbarossa makes Vladislaus II king of Bohemia.

title: Saladin
text: Saladin takes power in Egypt.

title: Legnano
text: The Lombard cities beat Barbarossa at Legnano.

title: The Margraviate of Moravia
text: Barbarossa makes Moravia a margraviate under the emperor, held by Conrad Otto.

title: Loditz
text: Bohemians and Moravians fight at Loditz; Moravia returns to Bohemia's rule.

title: Hattin
text: Saladin destroys the crusader army at Hattin and takes Jerusalem.

title: The Third Crusade
text: Barbarossa, Richard I and Philip II set out for the Holy Land.

title: Barbarossa drowns
text: Barbarossa drowns crossing the Saleph in Anatolia.

title: Premysl Ottokar returns
text: Premysl Ottokar takes the Bohemian throne, losing it again in 1193.

title: The massacre at Orvieto
text: The Encyclopaedia's massacre at Orvieto falls here.
ref: Real history; character from the Encyclopaedia entry linked, year a house reading

title: Henry VI's last year
text: Henry VI plans to make the empire hereditary; he dies at Messina the next year.

title: Pythagoras carries Thoth's lore west
text: Hermetic history says Pythagoras brought the lore of Thoth to the Greeks (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 20-21).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Hermes cults at war
text: For three centuries rival cults of Hermes murder and riot against each other in Greece and Egypt (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 22).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The council of twenty
text: About a century before Christ, twenty mystics meet to end the feuds of the Hermes cults (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 22).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: A fragment smuggled out
text: One fragment of Lilith's lore survives in writings smuggled out of the Roman siege of Jerusalem; the book prints the year as 64 (Revelations of the Dark Mother pdf 18).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

title: The Devil Kings
text: A dynasty of Infernalist mages takes hold of Arabia and Persia, and keeps it until 756 (Mage: The Dark Ages pdf 164).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The first Hollow Men
text: Fianna songs of Roman Britain first name the Hollow Men, the oldest breed of fomori (W20 Book of the Wyrm pdf 135).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Prophet's helpers
text: Some Batini later claim the Prophet had magical help (Mage: The Dark Ages pdf 40).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The covenants
text: By 700 the mages of Europe have gathered into covenants (Order of Hermes Revised pdf 26).
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Emperor Henry VI dies
text: Henry VI dies of fever at Messina; the empire falls into a contest between Philip of Swabia and Otto of Brunswick.

title: Innocent III elected pope
text: Lothar of Segni becomes Innocent III, the most powerful pope of the age, and soon calls a new crusade.

title: Two kings of the Romans
text: Rival princes elect Philip of Swabia and Otto IV; ten years of civil war follow across the German lands.

title: Ottokar I king of Bohemia
text: Premysl Ottokar I takes the title of king, which the Golden Bull of 1212 later confirms.

title: Richard the Lionheart dies
text: Richard I of England dies of a crossbow wound at the siege of Chalus; John takes the throne.

title: The Courts of Love take note
text: Philip II of France grows stronger against the English kings; the Toreador of the Grand Court watch the balance shift toward Paris.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The university of Paris chartered
text: Philip II grants the scholars of Paris rights against the city's officers, the start of the university's privileges.

title: Masters of the new university
text: Hermetic masters take rooms among the Paris scholars, and the craftsmen who will become the Order of Reason do the same.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Venice agrees to carry the crusade
text: The Treaty of Venice binds the Fourth Crusade to pay for a fleet it cannot afford.

title: Fibonacci's book of reckoning
text: Leonardo of Pisa publishes the Liber Abaci, bringing Hindu-Arabic numerals to European merchants.

title: The first crusader assault on Constantinople
text: Crusaders storm the city's sea walls and restore Isaac II and Alexios IV; the bargain cannot be paid.

title: The great fire of 1203
text: A fire set during fighting burns a broad swath of Constantinople; tens of thousands lose their homes.

title: Alexios V seizes the throne
text: Alexios Doukas Mourtzouphlos strangles Alexios IV and defies the crusaders.

title: Three days of sack
text: The crusaders break in and loot for three days; Cainites of every clan flee or burn with their havens, and the Dream ends.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Relics carried west
text: Relics, books and treasures from the sack flood into Venice, Paris and the Rhineland; mages hunt for the true ones among the fakes.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Empire of Nicaea
text: Theodore Laskaris gathers Byzantine refugees at Nicaea and founds a successor state.

title: The Empire of Trebizond
text: The Komnenos brothers found an empire on the Black Sea coast with Georgian help.

title: Normandy lost to France
text: Philip II takes Rouen and Normandy from King John.

title: Adrianople
text: The Bulgarian tsar Kaloyan destroys the Latin army and captures Emperor Baldwin I, who dies in prison.

title: The Delhi Sultanate
text: Qutb ud-Din Aibak, a slave general, founds the Mamluk dynasty of Delhi.

title: The khan's oath under the Eternal Blue Sky
text: Temujin is proclaimed Genghis Khan; the courts of the Middle Kingdom take the omens of the steppe seriously.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: England under interdict threat
text: Innocent III names Stephen Langton Archbishop of Canterbury against King John's wishes.

title: A legate murdered
text: The papal legate Peter of Castelnau is killed near Saint-Gilles; the pope calls a crusade against the Cathars.

title: England under interdict
text: The pope lays England under interdict: no masses, no church burials, for six years.

title: Francis of Assisi's first rule
text: Pope Innocent approves the brotherhood of Francis; the Franciscans begin.

title: Carcassonne falls
text: Simon de Montfort takes Carcassonne; inquirers ride with the army and learn which questions make people confess.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Aristotle banned
text: A council at Paris forbids lecturing on Aristotle's natural philosophy; the ban is widely ignored.

title: The Mongols attack the Jin
text: Genghis Khan invades the Jin empire and wins at Badger Mouth.

title: The Teutonic Knights in Transylvania
text: King Andrew II of Hungary settles the Teutonic Order in the Burzenland to guard the passes.

title: Las Navas de Tolosa
text: Christian kings of Spain crush the Almohads; the reconquest of al-Andalus speeds up.

title: The children's crusade passes
text: Bands of children and the poor march toward the sea; few come home, and some Kindred along the road grow fat.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Muret
text: Simon de Montfort kills Peter II of Aragon at Muret; the south loses its strongest protector.

title: Bouvines
text: Philip II beats Otto IV and his allies; John's hopes of retaking Normandy end, and Otto's empire collapses.

title: Zhongdu falls
text: The Mongols take the Jin capital (Beijing) and burn it for a month.

title: The Fourth Lateran Council
text: The council requires yearly confession, defines transubstantiation and orders Jews and Muslims to wear distinct dress.

title: King John dies
text: John dies during the barons' war; the boy Henry III is crowned and William Marshal rules for him.

title: The Dominicans approved
text: Pope Honorius III confirms the Order of Preachers founded by Dominic.

title: The Fair of Lincoln
text: William Marshal routs the French-backed rebels at Lincoln; Prince Louis gives up the English crown.

title: The Fifth Crusade sails
text: Crusaders gather at Acre, then turn on Egypt.

title: The Otrar killing
text: The governor of Otrar kills a Mongol trade caravan; Genghis Khan resolves on war with Khwarazm.

title: Damietta falls
text: The crusaders take Damietta after a long siege; disease has killed most of the city.

title: The riders cross the Jaxartes
text: The Mongol host enters Khwarazm; Garou of the Silk Road watch the land fill with ash and carrion spirits.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Samarkand falls
text: Samarkand surrenders and is plundered; its craftsmen are carried off to Mongolia.

title: The killing at Merv
text: Tolui's army takes Merv and kills nearly every inhabitant; chroniclers write of hundreds of thousands dead.

title: Nishapur destroyed
text: After a Mongol prince dies in its siege, Nishapur is razed and even its animals killed.

title: The Fifth Crusade ends
text: The crusaders, trapped by the Nile's flood, give up Damietta.

title: The Battle of the Indus
text: Jalal al-Din of Khwarazm escapes Genghis Khan by riding his horse into the river.

title: The Golden Bull of Hungary
text: Andrew II grants the Hungarian nobles their rights, including the right to resist an unjust king.

links.title: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

title: The university of Padua
text: Scholars leaving Bologna found a new school at Padua.

title: The Kalka
text: Mongol scouts under Subutai destroy the Rus princes on the Kalka; the Rus forget the warning, and the Shadow Lords do not.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Philip Augustus dies
text: Philip II of France dies after 43 years; Louis VIII takes the throne.

title: Frederick II founds Naples university
text: The emperor founds a school at Naples to train lawyers and officials for his kingdom.

title: The stigmata of Francis
text: Francis of Assisi is said to receive the wounds of Christ; the Messianic Voices count it a sign.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Magna Carta reissued
text: Henry III reissues Magna Carta in its lasting form in return for a tax.

title: Francis of Assisi dies
text: Francis dies at the Portiuncula; canonised two years later.

title: Louis VIII dies
text: The king dies on his way back from the Albigensian campaign; Blanche of Castile rules for the boy Louis IX.

title: Genghis Khan dies
text: Genghis Khan dies during the war on the Xi Xia, who are destroyed; the courts of the East mark the death of the scourge.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Bornhoved
text: North German princes break Danish power in the Baltic.

title: The Sixth Crusade
text: Excommunicated, Frederick II sails for the Holy Land anyway.

title: Jerusalem returned by treaty
text: Sultan al-Kamil hands Jerusalem to Frederick II by treaty, without a battle.

title: The Treaty of Paris
text: The Albigensian war ends; Toulouse submits and the Inquisition arrives in the south.

title: The council of Toulouse
text: A church council at Toulouse sets out how to search out heretics and bans the Bible in the common tongue.

title: Castile and Leon united
text: Ferdinand III unites the crowns of Castile and Leon for good.

title: The Teutonic crusade in Prussia
text: The Teutonic Knights begin their war against the pagan Prussians from Kulm.

title: Papal inquisitors
text: Gregory IX sends inquisitors answerable to the pope, most of them Dominicans.

title: The Constitutions of Melfi
text: Frederick II issues a law code for the Kingdom of Sicily.

title: Conrad of Marburg's hunt
text: Conrad of Marburg burns suspects across Germany; the shadow Inquisition in the Empire takes note of his methods.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Conrad of Marburg murdered
text: Knights kill the inquisitor on the road; his terror ends.

title: The end of the Jin
text: The Mongols and the Song take the last Jin city; the last Jin emperor dies.

title: Karakorum walled
text: Ogedei Khan builds walls and a palace at Karakorum, the Mongol capital.

title: Cordoba taken
text: Ferdinand III takes Cordoba; the great mosque becomes a cathedral.

title: The Mongols turn west
text: Batu and Subutai destroy Volga Bulgaria.

title: Ryazan burned
text: The first Rus city falls to Batu's host.

title: Vladimir falls
text: The Mongols take Vladimir and burn the grand prince's family in the cathedral.

title: The Sit River
text: Grand Prince Yuri II is killed and his army destroyed.

title: Valencia taken
text: James I of Aragon takes Valencia.

title: Frederick II excommunicated again
text: Pope and emperor go to open war in Italy.

title: The Neva
text: Prince Alexander of Novgorod beats a Swedish force and is called Nevsky.

title: Kiev falls
text: Batu's army storms Kiev; the mother of Rus cities is ruined, and Cainites who held it scatter.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Krakow burned
text: A Mongol column burns Krakow; legend says a trumpeter was shot mid-call from the church tower.

title: Legnica
text: The Mongols destroy Duke Henry II of Silesia's army, Teutonic and Templar knights among it.

title: Mohi
text: Batu and Subutai destroy the Hungarian army; King Bela IV flees to the Adriatic.

title: Ogedei dies and the horde turns back
text: Word of the great khan's death reaches the army in Hungary; the Mongols withdraw, and the Tzimisce and the Garou of the plains count their dead.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

title: Lubeck and Hamburg ally
text: The two cities agree to guard the road between them, the seed of the Hanseatic League.

title: The battle on the ice
text: Alexander Nevsky beats the Livonian Knights on frozen Lake Peipus.

title: The Golden Horde
text: Batu sets his capital at Sarai on the Volga; the Rus princes must travel there for leave to rule.

title: Kose Dag
text: The Mongols break the Seljuk sultanate of Rum.

title: The fall of Montsegur
text: More than two hundred Cathars are burned below the mountain fortress; the Inquisition calls it victory, and the Inquisition is wrong to call it the end.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Jerusalem sacked
text: Khwarazmian horsemen take and wreck Jerusalem.

links.title: Cainites under the Kingdom of Jerusalem
Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

title: La Forbie
text: An Egyptian and Khwarazmian army destroys the crusader host near Gaza.

title: Frederick II deposed
text: The Council of Lyon declares the emperor deposed.

title: A friar to the khan
text: John of Plano Carpini sets out for the Mongol court as the pope's envoy.

title: Guyuk enthroned
text: Guyuk becomes great khan with Carpini watching.

title: Seville taken
text: Ferdinand III takes Seville after a long siege.

title: Cologne cathedral begun
text: The foundation stone of the new cathedral is laid; it will not be finished for six hundred years.

title: The Sainte-Chapelle
text: Louis IX consecrates his glass chapel for the Crown of Thorns; the Celestial Chorus calls it a true house of the One.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Seventh Crusade lands
text: Louis IX takes Damietta again.

title: Mansourah
text: The crusaders break into Mansourah and are cut down in its streets by the Mamluks under Baibars.

title: Louis IX captured
text: The French king is taken prisoner and ransomed.

title: The Mamluks take Egypt
text: Mamluk officers kill the last Ayyubid sultan of Egypt.

title: Frederick II dies
text: The stupor mundi dies in Apulia; Hohenstaufen power soon collapses.

title: Mongke becomes great khan
text: After a bitter assembly Mongke is raised as great khan and purges Ogedei's line.

title: The gold florin
text: Florence strikes the gold florin, soon the standard coin of European trade.

title: William of Rubruck at Karakorum
text: The Flemish friar reaches the great khan's court and debates Buddhists, Muslims and Nestorians there.

title: The kingdom of Dali falls
text: Kublai conquers the kingdom of Dali in Yunnan.

title: The Great Interregnum
text: With Conrad IV dead, the empire has no accepted ruler for almost twenty years.

title: The Rhenish League
text: Rhineland towns band together to keep the peace on the river roads.

title: The Nizari castles surrender
text: Hulegu takes Alamut and the Nizari strongholds; Kindred in the east say the Assamites did not stir, because their Alamut is not this one.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

links.title: Gabriel Chavez, the Eyes of Alamut

title: The Sorbonne
text: Robert de Sorbon founds a college for poor theology students in Paris.

title: Baghdad sacked
text: The Mongols take Baghdad, kill the caliph and throw the libraries into the Tigris; Batini carry out what they can.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Provisions of Oxford
text: English barons force Henry III to share power with a council.

title: Rumi's poems
text: Jalal ad-Din Rumi begins the Masnavi at Konya.

title: The Treaty of Paris
text: Henry III gives up his claims to Normandy and Anjou and keeps Gascony as Louis IX's vassal.

title: Aleppo and Damascus fall
text: Hulegu takes Aleppo and Damascus; the Mamluks are next.

title: Ain Jalut
text: The Mamluks under Qutuz and Baibars beat the Mongols in Galilee; the mummies of Egypt call it a reprieve for the river.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Baibars becomes sultan
text: Baibars murders Qutuz on the road home and takes the throne.

title: Kressenbrunn
text: Ottokar II of Bohemia beats the Hungarians and takes Styria.

title: The flagellants
text: Bands of penitents whip themselves through the towns of Italy; the Church is unsure whether to bless them or hunt them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Kublai and Ariq Boke
text: Kublai and his brother Ariq Boke are both proclaimed great khan; civil war splits the empire.

title: The Byzantines take back the city
text: Michael VIII Palaiologos's general walks into Constantinople almost without a fight; Latin rule ends, but the Dream does not return.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Iceland under Norway
text: The Icelandic chieftains accept the Norwegian king.

title: Largs
text: Scots and storms drive off a Norwegian fleet; the Hebrides pass to Scotland three years later.

title: Lewes
text: Simon de Montfort captures Henry III and his son Edward.

title: Corpus Christi
text: Urban IV makes the feast of Corpus Christi a feast of the whole Church.

title: Montfort's parliament
text: Simon de Montfort calls knights and burgesses from towns to parliament.

title: Evesham
text: Prince Edward kills Simon de Montfort and cuts the body to pieces.

title: Benevento
text: Charles of Anjou kills King Manfred and takes Sicily and Naples.

title: Roger Bacon writes for the pope
text: Roger Bacon sends Clement IV his great work on experiment and optics; the craftsmen of the future Order of Reason study it.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Giotto born
text: The painter Giotto di Bondone is born near Florence.

title: The last Hohenstaufen
text: Charles of Anjou defeats Conradin, then beheads the sixteen-year-old in Naples.

title: Antioch destroyed
text: Baibars takes Antioch and kills or enslaves its people; the crusader principality ends.

title: Louis IX dies at Tunis
text: The Eighth Crusade ends when the French king dies of dysentery outside Tunis.

title: The Yuan dynasty
text: Kublai Khan proclaims the Great Yuan and builds a new capital at Khanbaliq (Beijing).

title: The Polos set out
text: Marco Polo leaves Venice with his father and uncle for the court of Kublai.

title: Krak des Chevaliers falls
text: The Hospitallers give up their great castle to Baibars.

title: Henry III dies
text: Edward I becomes king of England while still on crusade.

title: Rudolf of Habsburg elected
text: The German princes choose Rudolf of Habsburg as king, ending the interregnum.

title: Rumi dies
text: The poet dies at Konya; the whirling dervishes of the Mevlevi order grow from his followers.

title: Thomas Aquinas dies
text: Aquinas dies on the way to the Council of Lyon, his Summa unfinished.

title: The first Mongol fleet against Japan
text: A Mongol and Korean fleet lands at Hakata and then sails off in a storm; the kami are said to have answered.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Second Council of Lyon
text: The Greek envoys accept union with Rome; their church at home does not.

title: Hangzhou surrenders
text: The Song capital surrenders to the Mongol general Bayan.

title: The Paris condemnations
text: Bishop Tempier condemns 219 philosophical propositions, many drawn from Aristotle and Averroes.

title: Edward I invades Wales
text: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd is forced to terms.

title: The Marchfeld
text: Rudolf of Habsburg kills Ottokar II of Bohemia; Austria passes to the Habsburgs.

title: The fall of the Song
text: The last Song fleet is destroyed at Yamen and the boy emperor drowns; Kuei-jin speak of a turning of the age.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Albertus Magnus dies
text: The Dominican master of natural philosophy dies at Cologne.

title: The divine wind
text: A typhoon wrecks the second, far larger Mongol invasion of Japan; priests and spirits both claim the storm.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Sicilian Vespers
text: Palermo rises against the French at vespers on Easter Monday; Sicily passes to Aragon.

title: Llywelyn killed
text: The last native Prince of Wales dies in a skirmish; Wales is conquered.

title: Edward's castles
text: Edward I begins Caernarfon, Conwy and Harlech to hold Wales.

title: Prussia conquered
text: The Teutonic Knights finish the conquest of the Prussians.

title: Meloria
text: Genoa destroys the Pisan fleet; Pisa never recovers.

title: The children of Hamelin
text: One hundred and thirty children vanish from Hamelin; the town's records blame a piper, and the fae say nothing.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Philip the Fair
text: Philip IV becomes King of France.

title: St. Lucia's flood
text: A storm surge drowns tens of thousands along the Dutch and German coast.

title: Worringen
text: The burghers of Cologne and their allies break the archbishop's power.

title: Tripoli falls
text: The Mamluks take Tripoli in Lebanon.

title: The Jews expelled from England
text: Edward I orders all Jews out of England; they will not be readmitted for over three centuries.

title: Acre falls
text: The Mamluks storm Acre and the crusader kingdom ends; Kindred of the Military Orders sail for Cyprus with the survivors.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Swiss oath
text: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swear to defend each other, the start of the Swiss Confederation.

title: The Mongols in Java
text: A Mongol fleet lands in Java; the Majapahit state rises from the fighting.

title: Celestine V resigns
text: The hermit pope resigns after five months; Boniface VIII follows him.

title: Kublai Khan dies
text: The great khan dies; his empire no longer obeys one ruler.

title: Ghazan turns to Islam
text: The Ilkhan Ghazan becomes Muslim, and the Mongols of Persia follow.

title: Marco Polo returns
text: The Polos come home to Venice after twenty-four years.

title: Berwick sacked
text: Edward I takes Berwick and kills many of its people; Scotland is conquered.

title: Stirling Bridge
text: William Wallace and Andrew Moray destroy an English army.

title: Falkirk
text: Edward I breaks Wallace's army.

title: Marco Polo's book
text: A prisoner of Genoa, Marco Polo tells his travels to the writer Rustichello.

title: Osman's beylik
text: Osman's frontier state in Bithynia grows; the Ottomans take their name from him.

title: Wadi al-Khazandar
text: Ghazan's Mongols beat the Mamluks near Homs and briefly take Damascus.

title: The first Jubilee
text: Boniface VIII proclaims a holy year; pilgrims crowd Rome for full pardon of sins.

title: The Prague groschen
text: Wenceslas II reforms the Bohemian coinage on Kutna Hora silver.

title: Dante exiled
text: Dante Alighieri is banished from Florence and begins the Divine Comedy in exile.

title: The Bruges Matins
text: Flemish townsmen kill the French garrison of Bruges at dawn.

title: The Golden Spurs
text: Flemish militia destroy the French knights at Courtrai.

title: Unam Sanctam
text: Boniface VIII declares that every creature must be subject to the pope.

title: Bapheus
text: Osman beats a Byzantine army, his first great victory.

title: The outrage at Anagni
text: Philip the Fair's men seize Boniface VIII; the pope dies weeks later.

title: Marj al-Saffar
text: The Mamluks beat Ghazan's last invasion of Syria.

title: The courts make peace
text: In the year the Quincunx is signed, mortal China lies quiet under the Yuan; the courts take it as proof the treaty works.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Wallace executed
text: William Wallace is hanged, drawn and quartered at Smithfield.

title: Robert the Bruce crowned
text: Robert Bruce kills a rival and is crowned King of Scots.

title: The Jews expelled from France
text: Philip IV expels the Jews from France and takes their goods.

title: The last Premyslid
text: Wenceslas III is murdered at Olomouc; the Bohemian royal line ends.

title: The Templars arrested
text: On Friday 13 October Philip IV has every Templar in France seized; some say Cainite counsellors or Batini with grudges guided the king.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Edward I dies
text: Edward I dies on his way north to fight Bruce; Edward II takes the throne.

title: Danzig taken
text: The Teutonic Knights seize Danzig and kill many of its people.

title: The popes at Avignon
text: Clement V settles in Avignon; the popes will stay for nearly seventy years, and the Kindred of Rome lose their nearest grip on the Church.

title: Marienburg
text: The Teutonic grand master moves to Marienburg, the largest brick castle in Europe.

text: The Knights of St John make Rhodes their island base.

title: The Council of Vienne

text: Clement V dissolves the Order of the Temple and gives its lands to the Hospitallers.

title: Henry VII dies in Italy
text: The emperor dies of fever, ending hopes of restoring imperial rule in Italy.

text: Scottish nobles ask the pope to recognise their independence.

text: Dante dies in exile at Ravenna, the Comedy complete.

text: Louis of Bavaria captures his rival Frederick of Austria.

title: Mansa Musa in Cairo
text: Mansa Musa passes through Cairo with so much gold that its price falls for years.

title: Alice Kyteler tried

title: Ibn Battuta sets out
text: Ibn Battuta leaves Tangier on pilgrimage and travels for nearly thirty years.

ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Bursa taken
text: Orhan takes Bursa and makes it the Ottoman capital.

title: Edward II murdered
text: The deposed king dies in prison; Edward III, fourteen, takes the throne.

title: The Valois
text: Charles IV dies without a son; Philip VI of Valois takes the crown, and Edward III's claim waits.

title: Cassel
text: Philip VI crushes the Flemish rising.

title: Louis of Bavaria crowned in Rome
text: Louis IV is crowned emperor by the Roman people and sets up an antipope.

title: Pelekanos
text: Orhan beats the Byzantine emperor in Bithynia.

ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Nicaea falls
text: The Ottomans take Nicaea.

title: Plague in China
text: An epidemic kills many in Hebei; some historians see the first sign of the Black Death.

title: The Genko War
text: Emperor Go-Daigo rises against the Kamakura shogunate.

title: Kamakura falls
text: Nitta Yoshisada takes Kamakura; the Hojo regents kill themselves and the shogunate ends.

title: Halidon Hill
text: Edward III's archers destroy a Scottish army.

title: The Arno flood
text: The Arno sweeps away Florence's bridges.

title: Giotto's bell tower
text: Giotto begins the campanile of Florence cathedral.

title: The Ilkhanate breaks up
text: Abu Said dies without an heir; Mongol Persia falls apart.

title: Two courts in Japan
text: Ashikaga Takauji takes Kyoto; Go-Daigo flees to Yoshino, and the Northern and Southern courts begin.

title: Vijayanagara founded
text: Harihara and Bukka found the empire of Vijayanagara in southern India.

title: The Hundred Years War begins
text: Philip VI confiscates Gascony; Edward III claims the French crown.

title: Giotto dies
text: The painter who changed Italian art dies in Florence.

title: The Ashikaga shogunate
text: Ashikaga Takauji becomes shogun.

title: The Declaration of Rhens
text: The electors declare that the man they choose is king without the pope's leave.

title: Venice and Florence fight Verona
text: Venice expands on the mainland at Verona's cost.

title: Sluys
text: The English destroy the French fleet off Flanders.

title: Rio Salado
text: Castile and Portugal beat the last great Marinid invasion of Spain.

title: Byzantine civil war
text: A civil war between John Kantakouzenos and the regency of John V begins; both sides hire Turks.

title: The Breton war of succession
text: England and France fight over Brittany through rival dukes.

title: The Magdalene flood
text: The worst recorded flood in central Europe sweeps the Rhine, Main and Danube.

title: The Bardi and Peruzzi fall
text: The great Florentine banks begin to fail after Edward III defaults on his loans.

title: St. George's Night rising
text: Estonian peasants rise against German lords and are crushed.

title: Smyrna taken
text: A crusader league takes the harbour of Smyrna from the Turks.

title: Florence bankrupt
text: The Bardi bank collapses, taking much of Florence's wealth with it.

title: Revolt in the Deccan
text: The Bahmani nobles break the Deccan away from Delhi; the Bahmani sultanate is founded in 1347.

title: Crecy
text: English longbowmen cut down the French knights; the blind King John of Bohemia dies in the charge.

title: Neville's Cross
text: The English capture David II of Scotland.

title: Plague at Caffa
text: The Mongol army besieging Caffa in the Crimea is struck by plague; Genoese ships will carry it west.

title: Calais besieged
text: Edward III begins an eleven-month siege of Calais.

title: Vladislaus gives way
text: Vladislaus Henry yields Bohemia to his brother Ottokar and takes Moravia as margrave.

title: Minamoto no Yoritomo dies
text: The first Kamakura shogun dies after a fall from a horse; the Hojo family begin to rule for his heirs.

title: The Hojo regency
text: Hojo Tokimasa becomes regent to the shogun, and the regents rule Japan in fact.

title: Henry of Flanders
text: Henry of Flanders becomes Latin emperor and rules the conquered lands with skill.

title: Muhammad of Ghor killed
text: The conqueror of northern India is murdered on the Indus; his generals divide the empire.

title: Scholars at Cambridge
text: Scholars fleeing a riot at Oxford settle at Cambridge.

title: Iltutmish
text: Iltutmish takes the throne of Delhi and holds northern India against the Mongols.

title: Queen Gertrude murdered
text: Hungarian nobles kill Andrew II's queen for favouring her German kin.

links.title: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

title: Innocent III dies

title: The Danish flag
text: Danes conquering Estonia win at Lyndanisse; legend says the Danish flag fell from the sky.

title: Frederick II crowned emperor
text: Pope Honorius III crowns Frederick II in Rome.

title: Salisbury cathedral begun
text: Work begins on the new cathedral at Salisbury.

title: The Franciscan rule
text: The pope approves the final rule of the Franciscans.

title: Tartu taken
text: The Livonian crusaders take Tartu; the Get of Fenris and the Shadow Lords of the Baltic mark the last pagan groves burning.

title: The Tran dynasty
text: The Tran family takes the throne of Dai Viet.

title: Gregory IX
text: Ugolino of Segni becomes pope and excommunicates Frederick II within months.

title: Frederick lands at Acre
text: The excommunicated emperor reaches the Holy Land.

title: The Mongols invade Goryeo
text: The first of many Mongol invasions of Korea begins.

title: The Korean court flees to Ganghwa
text: The Goryeo court moves to Ganghwa Island and holds out there for decades.

title: Kaifeng and the thunder crash bombs
text: The Jin defend Kaifeng with gunpowder bombs and fire lances; plague kills hundreds of thousands in the city.

title: Razia Sultana
text: Razia becomes Sultan of Delhi, the only woman to rule it.

title: The Livonian Order
text: The Sword Brothers, beaten by the Lithuanians, join the Teutonic Order as its Livonian branch.

title: The Tzimisce look east
text: Word of the riders in the Rus lands reaches the voivodes of the Carpathians; most do not believe it.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Nasrids of Granada
text: Muhammad I founds the Nasrid kingdom of Granada, the last Muslim state in Spain.

title: Chernigov falls
text: The Mongols take Chernigov and Pereyaslavl.

title: The Tatar Yoke begins
text: The Rus princes submit to the Golden Horde; the Shadow Lords' quiet backing of the Mongols begins.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Pest burned
text: After Mohi the Mongols burn Pest and range across Hungary all summer.

title: The Mongols in Moravia
text: A Mongol column crosses Moravia, burning villages and failing before Olomouc.

title: The Mongols at the Adriatic
text: Mongol riders chase King Bela to the coast at Trogir.

title: Innocent IV
text: The new pope flees to Lyon to escape Frederick II.

title: The friars' mission to the Mongols
text: The Council of Lyon sends friars east to learn what the Mongols want.

title: The last Babenberg
text: Duke Frederick of Austria dies in battle; Austria is left without a lord.

title: The Sakya lama and the Mongols
text: Sakya Pandita submits Tibet to Godan Khan, the first tie between Tibet and the Mongols.

title: The Brotherhood watches the Mongols
text: The Akashic Brotherhood in Tibet watches the lamas bargain with the khans and keeps its own counsel.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Iglau mining law
text: The silver town of Jihlava writes down its mining code.

title: The stone castles
text: Bela IV orders stone castles built across Hungary against the Mongols' return.

links.title: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

title: Ottokar takes Austria
text: Ottokar of Bohemia takes Austria and marries the Babenberg heiress.

title: King Mindaugas
text: Mindaugas of Lithuania is baptised and crowned, though Lithuania stays pagan.

title: Ottokar II king
text: Premysl Ottokar II becomes King of Bohemia, the iron and golden king.

title: Konigsberg founded
text: The Teutonic Knights found Konigsberg, named for Ottokar of Bohemia.

title: Nichiren preaches
text: The monk Nichiren preaches that the Lotus Sutra alone can save Japan.

title: Two foreign kings
text: The electors choose both Richard of Cornwall and Alfonso X of Castile.

title: The caliph is trampled
text: Hulegu has the last Abbasid caliph rolled in a carpet and trampled; the Cainites of Baghdad who lived through the sack go into the desert.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Mongke dies at Diaoyu
text: The great khan dies besieging a Song fortress; the Mongol armies in Syria and China pause.

title: Korea submits
text: The Goryeo crown prince submits to the Mongols.

title: A caliph in Cairo
text: Baibars sets up an Abbasid survivor as caliph in Cairo to bless Mamluk rule.

title: Alexander Nevsky dies
text: The prince dies returning from the Horde.

title: Caesarea and Arsuf
text: Baibars takes the crusader towns of the coast one by one.

title: Safed
text: Baibars takes Safed from the Templars and kills the garrison.

title: The Phags-pa script
text: Kublai adopts a new script for all the empire's languages.

title: The Sambyeolcho revolt
text: Korean soldiers who will not submit to the Mongols hold out on Jeju until 1273.

title: Xiangyang falls
text: Persian engineers' counterweight trebuchets end a five-year siege; the road into southern China is open.

title: The Messianic Voices at Lyon
text: Bonaventure dies during the council; the Messianic Voices lose a friend in the Church's councils.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Ottokar gives up Austria
text: Rudolf of Habsburg forces Ottokar II to surrender Austria and Styria.

title: King Dinis
text: Dinis of Portugal plants pine forests and founds the university at Lisbon.

title: The Shoushi calendar
text: Guo Shoujing's astronomers produce the most exact calendar yet made.

title: The second battle of Homs
text: The Mamluks beat the Mongols and their Armenian and Georgian allies.

title: The stolen children are not found
text: No one finds Hamelin's children; changelings in the German lands keep the tale close.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Venice and Genoa fight at Acre
text: The Italian quarters of Acre are at war with each other.

title: Alexander III dies
text: The king of Scots falls from his horse in a storm; Scotland is left with a child queen in Norway.

title: Pagan falls
text: A Mongol army ends the kingdom of Pagan in Burma.

title: Bach Dang
text: Tran Hung Dao destroys a Mongol fleet on staked river beds in Vietnam.

title: The Maid of Norway dies
text: The child queen of Scotland dies on her way from Norway; Edward I is asked to judge between the claimants.

title: John Balliol
text: Edward I picks John Balliol as King of Scots.

title: Majapahit founded
text: Raden Wijaya uses the Mongols to destroy a rival, then drives them out and founds Majapahit.

title: Alauddin Khalji
text: Alauddin Khalji murders his uncle and takes Delhi; he will beat back several Mongol invasions.

title: The Grimaldi take Monaco
text: Francesco Grimaldi, disguised as a monk, seizes the rock of Monaco.

title: A new frontier state
text: Osman's beylik grows on the Byzantine border; Kindred of the Bosporus do not yet think it worth watching.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Arpad line ends
text: Andrew III dies; the Arpad kings of Hungary are gone.

links.title: Hungary and the Slavic East in 1230

title: Chittor
text: Alauddin Khalji takes the Rajput fortress of Chittor.

title: A Gascon pope
text: Bertrand de Got becomes Clement V and never goes to Rome.

title: King Albert murdered
text: Albert of Habsburg is killed by his nephew.

title: John of Luxembourg in Bohemia
text: John of Luxembourg marries the Premyslid heiress and is chosen King of Bohemia.

title: Al-Nasir Muhammad
text: The Mamluk sultan's third reign begins; Cairo reaches its height.

title: Philip the Fair dies
text: The king dies after a hunting fall, months after de Molay's death.

title: The pope fears sorcery
text: John XXII believes enemies tried to kill him with wax images; trials for sorcery follow.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Sweden and Norway joined
text: Magnus Eriksson inherits both crowns as a child.

title: Wladyslaw the Elbow-High
text: Wladyslaw is crowned King of Poland at Krakow, reuniting the kingdom.

title: The Tughluqs
text: Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq takes Delhi.

title: Vilnius
text: Grand Duke Gediminas invites merchants and craftsmen to Vilnius, his new capital.

title: Magic made heresy
text: John XXII declares that sorcery is heresy, giving inquisitors power over it.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Bohemia takes Silesia
text: John of Luxembourg brings the Silesian dukes under the Bohemian crown.

title: Moscow becomes the seat
text: Ivan Kalita becomes Grand Prince with the Horde's blessing, and the metropolitan moves to Moscow.

title: Posada
text: The Wallachians under Basarab ambush and destroy a Hungarian army in the Carpathians.

title: Stefan Dusan
text: Stefan Dusan takes the Serbian throne and builds the greatest Serbian state.

title: Casimir the Great
text: Casimir III becomes King of Poland and builds the country in stone.

title: The Madurai sultanate
text: The governor of Madurai breaks from Delhi.

title: The congress of Visegrad
text: The kings of Hungary, Poland and Bohemia meet at Visegrad and agree on trade and borders.

title: Plague in the steppe
text: Graves of Christian merchants near Lake Issyk-Kul record a pestilence; Garou far to the west smell something coming.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Casimir takes Galicia
text: Poland begins to take Galicia-Volhynia.

title: Ibn Battuta in Delhi
text: The traveller serves Muhammad bin Tughluq as a judge.

title: Plans for a new capital
text: Charles of Luxembourg, already ruling Bohemia for his father, plans to make Prague a capital; the Ventrue of the Empire take interest.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: St. Vitus begun
text: Work begins on the new cathedral of St. Vitus in Prague.

title: Jacob van Artevelde killed
text: The leader of Ghent is murdered by a mob.

title: Charles IV elected
text: Charles of Luxembourg is chosen King of the Romans against Louis of Bavaria.

title: Dusan emperor
text: Stefan Dusan is crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks.

title: Calais surrenders
text: Calais yields to Edward III after eleven months; the burghers offer their lives and are spared.

title: Plague ships at Messina
text: Genoese galleys bring the plague to Sicily; the Second Great Maelstrom gathers as the dead cross in numbers no one has seen.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Plague in Constantinople
text: The pestilence reaches Constantinople; the emperor's son is among the dead.

links.title: The great schism and the Paladins

title: Cola di Rienzo
text: The notary Cola di Rienzo takes power in Rome as tribune of the people.

title: The Bahmani sultanate
text: The Deccan nobles found the Bahmani sultanate at Gulbarga.

title: Plague in Marseille
text: The plague comes ashore in Provence and moves up the Rhone.

title: Plague in Florence
text: Perhaps half of Florence dies; Boccaccio sets the Decameron among young people fleeing it.

title: Charles University
text: Charles IV founds the first university north of the Alps in Prague.

title: Plague in England
text: The plague lands at a Dorset port and reaches London by autumn.

title: Plague in Cairo
text: The plague reaches Cairo; at its height thousands die a day.

title: Plague in Damascus
text: The people of Damascus fast and pray together, Muslims, Christians and Jews.

title: The pope sits between fires
text: Clement VI's physician keeps the pope between two great fires; the pope survives and buys Avignon outright.

title: The Stygian ferries overflow
text: The Hierarchy cannot ferry the dead fast enough; whole towns' worth of wraiths wander the Shadowlands unclaimed.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Kindred in the plague
text: Kindred who feed on the sick sicken their herds and sometimes the Masquerade; some princes forbid feeding in plague houses.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Friuli earthquake
text: An earthquake shakes the eastern Alps; preachers say it opened the earth for the plague.

title: The Strasbourg massacre
text: Hundreds of Jews are burned in Strasbourg on the charge of poisoning wells, before the plague even arrives.

title: The flagellants march
text: Processions of flagellants cross Germany; the pope condemns them in October.

title: Mainz and Cologne
text: The Jewish communities of the Rhineland are destroyed.

title: Plague in Norway
text: A ship brings the plague to Bergen; Norway loses perhaps half its people.

title: Plague in Moravia
text: The plague reaches Moravia, lighter than in the west but bad in the towns.

title: The Ordinance of Labourers
text: Edward III forbids wages above the old rates; there are too few hands left to obey.

title: Physicians and pestilence
text: Hermetic healers and Chorus monks die tending the sick; the young Order of Reason studies the plague's spread.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Shattering
text: Banality closes the trods to Arcadia; fae who stay must hide in mortal bodies.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Alfonso XI dies of plague
text: The king of Castile dies of plague at the siege of Gibraltar.

title: The second Jubilee
text: Pilgrims crowd Rome despite the plague.

title: Ayutthaya founded
text: King Ramathibodi founds Ayutthaya in Siam.

title: Les Espagnols sur Mer
text: The English beat a Castilian fleet in the Channel.

title: The Red Turbans
text: The Red Turban rebellion against the Yuan begins in the Huai valley.

title: The Statute of Treasons
text: Parliament defines high treason.

title: Muhammad bin Tughluq dies
text: The Delhi sultan who moved his capital and made copper coins worth silver dies on campaign.

title: The Ottomans in Europe
text: The Ottomans take the fortress of Tzympe on the Gallipoli peninsula, their first foothold in Europe.

title: The Decameron
text: Boccaccio finishes the Decameron.

title: Gallipoli after the earthquake
text: An earthquake shatters Gallipoli's walls; the Ottomans move in and settle the town.

title: Roderigo al-Dakhil
text: In the plague years Cairo's Kindred shift and shuffle; newcomers find room where the dead left gaps.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Cola di Rienzo killed
text: The returned tribune is killed by a Roman mob.

title: Charles IV crowned emperor
text: Charles IV is crowned in Rome and leaves the same day, as promised.

title: St. Scholastica's Day riot
text: A tavern brawl at Oxford becomes a two-day battle; dozens of students die.

title: Doge Faliero beheaded
text: The doge of Venice is beheaded for plotting to make himself lord of the city.

title: The Golden Bull of 1356
text: Charles IV fixes the seven electors and the rules for choosing a king.

title: Poitiers
text: The Black Prince captures King John II of France.

title: The Screaming Ghost Purge
text: The war between Dalou'laoshi, the Wu Lung and the Akashics begins; it will drive the Brotherhood back into Tibet by 1360.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Basel earthquake
text: The strongest recorded earthquake in central Europe wrecks Basel.

title: Etienne Marcel
text: The provost of Paris merchants forces reforms on the dauphin.

title: The Jacquerie
text: The peasants of northern France rise against the nobles and are crushed within weeks.

title: Etienne Marcel killed
text: The Paris leader is killed as he tries to open the city to Charles of Navarre.

title: Charles Bridge planned
text: Charles IV plans a new stone bridge across the Vltava; it is begun in 1357.

title: The Treaty of Bretigny
text: England gives up its claim to France in return for Aquitaine and Calais.

title: The Brotherhood withdraws
text: The Screaming Ghost Purge ends; the Akashics withdraw into Tibet.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The second pestilence
text: The plague returns, killing many children born since 1348.

title: Adrianople taken
text: Murad I takes Adrianople; as Edirne it becomes the Ottoman capital.

title: Lake Poyang
text: Zhu Yuanzhang destroys his chief rival's fleet in one of the largest naval battles ever fought.

title: Krakow university
text: Casimir the Great founds a university at Krakow.

title: Vienna university
text: Rudolf IV founds a university at Vienna.

title: Alexandria sacked
text: Peter I of Cyprus sacks Alexandria for a week.

title: The Statutes of Kilkenny
text: The English lords of Ireland are forbidden to marry, speak or dress as the Irish do.

title: Najera
text: The Black Prince wins for Pedro the Cruel in Castile.

title: The Ming
text: Zhu Yuanzhang founds the Ming and drives the Mongols out of Khanbaliq.

title: The courts and the Ming
text: The courts of the Middle Kingdom hold that the Quincunx kept their quarrels from spoiling the change of dynasty.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Pedro the Cruel killed
text: Pedro of Castile is stabbed by his half-brother Henry, who takes the throne.

title: Timur
text: Timur becomes master of Transoxiana.

title: Limoges sacked
text: The Black Prince storms Limoges; chroniclers tell of thousands killed.

title: The Peace of Stralsund
text: The Hanseatic towns force Denmark to yield; the League is at its height.

title: The Maritsa
text: The Ottomans destroy the Serbian lords of Macedonia.

title: The Stewarts
text: Robert II, the first Stewart, becomes King of Scots.

title: La Rochelle
text: A Castilian fleet destroys the English off La Rochelle.

title: Petrarch dies
text: The poet who first called the past ages dark dies near Padua.

title: The dancing plague
text: Crowds dance in the streets of Aachen and along the Rhine for days; priests try to cast out what moves them.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Boccaccio dies
text: The author of the Decameron dies at Certaldo.

title: The Black Prince dies
text: Edward III's heir dies of a long sickness.

title: The Good Parliament
text: The Commons impeach the king's ministers for the first time.

title: The pope returns to Rome
text: Gregory XI leaves Avignon for Rome.

title: Edward III dies
text: Richard II, ten years old, becomes king.

title: Jikji printed
text: A Korean Buddhist text is printed with movable metal type at Cheongju.

title: The Great Schism
text: Rival popes in Rome and Avignon divide Western Christendom for forty years.

title: The Ciompi
text: The wool workers of Florence rise and briefly take power.

title: Charles IV dies
text: The emperor dies in Prague; Wenceslas IV becomes king.

title: Wycliffe attacks the Church
text: John Wycliffe denies that the bread of the mass changes; the Messianic Voices and the Order of Reason both read him closely.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Kulikovo
text: Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow beats the Horde's general Mamai on the Don.

title: Chioggia
text: Venice breaks a Genoese siege of the lagoon and wins its long war.

title: Charles V dies
text: The wise king of France dies; Charles VI, eleven, follows.

title: The Peasants' Revolt
text: Wat Tyler's rebels take London; that same year young Kindred across the west rise against their elders, and the Anarch Revolt begins.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Wat Tyler killed
text: The rebel leader is killed at Smithfield in front of the king.

title: Tokhtamysh burns Moscow
text: The khan of the Horde sacks and burns Moscow.

title: Roosebeke
text: The French crush the Flemish towns.

title: Wycliffe dies
text: Wycliffe dies of a stroke; his followers, the Lollards, carry on.

title: Aljubarrota
text: Portugal beats Castile and keeps its independence.

title: The Union of Krewo
text: Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania agrees to marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland and be baptised.

title: Sempach
text: The Swiss destroy an Austrian army and kill its duke.

title: Heidelberg university
text: The Elector Palatine founds a university at Heidelberg.

title: Jogaila crowned
text: Jogaila is baptised as Wladyslaw and crowned King of Poland; Lithuania is baptised.

title: The Canterbury Tales
text: Geoffrey Chaucer begins the Canterbury Tales.

title: The last pagan state baptised
text: Lithuania's baptism closes the last great pagan country in Europe; Kindred who kept the old gods' shrines go deeper into the forests.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Otterburn
text: The Scots beat the English in the borders; Douglas dies winning.

title: Kosovo Field
text: Serbs and Ottomans fight at Kosovo; both Prince Lazar and Sultan Murad die.

text: The French Estates meet for the last time until 1789.

title: Osaka falls
text: The Tokugawa storm Osaka castle and destroy the Toyotomi family; Japan has one master.

title: Shakespeare dies
text: Shakespeare and Cervantes die in the same spring.

title: Copernicus banned
text: The Church puts Copernicus's book on the Index until it is corrected, and warns Galileo not to teach it as truth.

title: The Later Jin
text: Nurhaci proclaims the Later Jin, the start of the Qing.

title: The defenestration of 1618
text: The emperor's regents are thrown from a window of Prague castle; the Thirty Years War begins.

title: The Bohemian revolt
text: The Bohemian estates raise an army, take over the government and send envoys to every Protestant prince.

title: The Winter King
text: The Bohemians choose Frederick of the Palatinate as king.

title: Batavia
text: The Dutch take Jakarta and name it Batavia.

title: White Mountain
text: The Bohemian army is routed outside Prague in an hour; the Winter King flees and Bohemia's independence ends for three centuries.

title: The Mayflower sails
text: English separatists sail on the Mayflower for America to worship as they choose.

title: The Old Town Square executions
text: Twenty-seven leaders of the revolt are executed in Prague.

title: The truce ends
text: The war between Spain and the Dutch resumes.

title: The Anabaptists expelled
text: The Hutterite communities are driven out of Moravia; many go to Hungary and Transylvania.

title: The Amboyna massacre
text: The Dutch torture and kill English traders on Ambon.

title: Shah Abbas takes Baghdad
text: Shah Abbas takes Baghdad from the Ottomans and holds it fifteen years.

title: Richelieu
text: Cardinal Richelieu becomes chief minister of France and sets about breaking the Huguenots and the Habsburgs.

title: Charles I
text: Charles I becomes king of England and soon quarrels with Parliament over money and religion.

title: Dessau Bridge
text: Wallenstein beats Mansfeld's Protestant army at the Dessau bridge on the Elbe.

title: The Renewed Land Ordinance
text: Bohemia becomes Catholic by law; Protestants must convert or leave.

title: La Rochelle
text: Richelieu besieges the Huguenot port; it starves into surrender.

title: Moravia made Catholic
text: The Renewed Land Ordinance comes to Moravia; Protestants must convert or leave, and many lords go into exile.

title: Comenius leaves
text: The teacher and bishop of the Unity of Brethren, Jan Amos Comenius, leaves for exile in Poland and never returns.

title: The Edict of Restitution
text: The emperor orders all church lands taken since 1552 given back; the Protestant princes are driven toward Sweden.

title: The Bamberg trials
text: The prince-bishop of Bamberg burns hundreds as witches.

title: Gustavus Adolphus lands
text: Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden lands in Pomerania and enters the war on the Protestant side.

title: The Milan plague
text: Plague kills perhaps half of Milan; the city hunts for anointers said to spread it with ointment.

title: The sack of Magdeburg
text: Tilly's army storms Magdeburg; twenty thousand die in the sack and fire, and the city is a byword for horror.

title: Breitenfeld
text: Gustavus Adolphus destroys Tilly's army at Breitenfeld and the road into southern Germany is open.

title: Mumtaz Mahal dies
text: Shah Jahan's wife dies; he begins the Taj Mahal.

title: Vesuvius erupts
text: Vesuvius erupts after centuries of quiet and kills several thousand people around Naples.

title: Lutzen
text: Gustavus Adolphus dies leading a cavalry charge in the fog at Lutzen, though the Swedes win the field.

title: Galileo's Dialogue
text: Galileo publishes his Dialogue on the two world systems.

title: Galileo tried
text: The Roman Inquisition forces Galileo to recant his teaching that the earth moves; he spends his last years under house arrest.

title: Wallenstein murdered
text: The emperor's general Wallenstein, suspected of treason, is killed by his own officers at Cheb.

title: Nordlingen
text: The Swedes and their allies are destroyed at Nordlingen; France prepares to enter the war openly.

title: The Peace of Prague
text: The emperor makes peace with Saxony and most Lutheran princes; the war goes on, now a contest of France and the Habsburgs.

title: The French Academy
text: Richelieu founds the Academie francaise to guard the French language.

title: The Qing
text: Hong Taiji renames his Later Jin state the Great Qing and his people the Manchu.

title: Descartes's Discourse
text: Descartes publishes the Discourse on Method: I think, therefore I am.

title: Tulip mania
text: The price of tulip bulbs in Holland collapses overnight, ruining speculators.

title: The Shimabara rising
text: Christian peasants of Shimabara and Amakusa rise against taxes and persecution in Kyushu.

title: Baghdad retaken
text: Sultan Murad IV takes Baghdad back from Persia and kills much of its garrison.

title: Hara castle
text: The Shimabara rebels are killed to the last.

title: Japan closed
text: Japan expels the Portuguese and closes its ports.

title: The Treaty of Zuhab
text: The Ottomans and Persia sign the Treaty of Zuhab, fixing a border that lasts nearly to modern times.

title: Portugal free
text: Portugal rises, crowns the Duke of Braganza and breaks from sixty years of Spanish rule.

title: The Reapers' War
text: The reapers of Catalonia kill the viceroy and rise against Madrid; the war lasts twelve years.

title: The Irish rising
text: Irish Catholics rise against English and Scottish settlers; thousands die and the tales grow in the telling.

title: The English Civil War
text: King and Parliament raise armies and fight at Edgehill; the English Civil War has begun.

title: The Swedes take Olomouc
text: Swedish troops take Olomouc and hold it as their base in Moravia until 1650.

title: Richelieu dies
text: Richelieu dies; Cardinal Mazarin takes his place at the young king's side.

title: Rocroi
text: The French destroy the famed Spanish infantry at Rocroi.

title: Louis XIV
text: The four-year-old Louis XIV becomes king of France, with his mother and Mazarin to rule for him.

title: The Ming fall
text: Li Zicheng takes Beijing; the last Ming emperor hangs himself.

title: The Qing take Beijing
text: Wu Sangui opens the pass; the Manchus take China.

title: Marston Moor
text: Cromwell's cavalry win the north for Parliament at Marston Moor.

title: Brno holds
text: The Swedes besiege Brno for months and fail; the town is honoured for it ever after.

title: Naseby
text: Parliament's New Model Army destroys the king's army.

title: The Yangzhou massacre
text: Qing troops kill much of the population of Yangzhou in ten days after it resists them.

title: The Witchfinder General
text: Matthew Hopkins hangs about a hundred people as witches in East Anglia.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The war for Crete
text: The Ottomans invade Venetian Crete; the war lasts a generation.

title: Masaniello
text: The fisherman Masaniello leads Naples against Spanish taxes.

title: The Peace of Westphalia
text: The Thirty Years War ends; the Dutch are free.

title: The Swedes at Prague
text: Swedish troops take Prague castle and loot Rudolf's collections.

title: Khmelnytsky
text: The Cossacks rise against Poland; tens of thousands of Jews are killed.

title: The Fronde
text: Paris rises against Mazarin and the court flees the city; the Fronde lasts five years.

title: Sultan Ibrahim deposed
text: The mad Sultan Ibrahim is deposed and strangled; his seven-year-old son takes the throne.

title: Charles I beheaded
text: Charles I is beheaded outside his own Banqueting House in Whitehall.

title: Drogheda
text: Cromwell's army storms Drogheda and kills the garrison and many townspeople.

title: The Ulozhenie
text: Russia's law code binds peasants to the land.

title: The Swedes leave Olomouc
text: The Swedish garrison marches out of Olomouc after eight years, leaving a ruined town.

title: Leviathan
text: Thomas Hobbes publishes Leviathan: without a strong sovereign, life is nasty, brutish and short.

title: Worcester
text: Cromwell beats Charles II, who escapes by hiding in an oak.

title: Patriarch Nikon
text: Patriarch Nikon's reforms of Russian worship split the church; the Old Believers refuse them.

title: The Anglo-Dutch War
text: England and the Dutch Republic go to war at sea over trade.

title: The Taj Mahal finished
text: The Taj Mahal is finished at Agra as Shah Jahan's tomb for his wife.

title: Lord Protector
text: Oliver Cromwell becomes Lord Protector of England, Scotland and Ireland.

title: Pereyaslav
text: At Pereyaslav the Cossacks of Ukraine swear loyalty to the tsar.

title: The Deluge
text: Sweden invades Poland; the years of war that follow are remembered as the Deluge.

title: The Naples plague
text: Plague kills perhaps half of Naples in a single summer.

title: The Koprulu viziers
text: Mehmed Koprulu becomes grand vizier and saves the empire.

title: Cromwell dies
text: Oliver Cromwell dies; his son cannot hold power.

title: Aurangzeb
text: Aurangzeb imprisons his father and takes the throne.

title: The Peace of the Pyrenees
text: France and Spain make peace at the Pyrenees; Louis XIV will marry the Spanish infanta.

title: The Restoration
text: Charles II returns to London and the monarchy is restored.

title: The Royal Society
text: The Royal Society is founded in London for the advancement of natural knowledge by experiment.

title: Louis rules himself
text: Mazarin dies and Louis XIV announces that he will rule without a chief minister.

title: Kangxi
text: The Kangxi emperor takes the Qing throne as a child; he will rule sixty-one years.

title: Koxinga takes Taiwan
text: The Ming loyalist Koxinga drives the Dutch from Taiwan.

title: The Tatar raid
text: Ottoman Tatars raid Moravia and carry off thousands.

title: Szentgotthard
text: Imperial and French troops beat an Ottoman army at Szentgotthard.

title: The Great Plague
text: Plague kills perhaps a hundred thousand Londoners, a quarter of the city.

title: Kindred of the plague city
text: Prince Mithras's Kindred hunt among the dying while the court flees to Oxford.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Great Fire
text: London burns for four days; Kindred lose havens in the City, and some say a few of them lit the fire.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: Sabbatai Zevi
text: The messianic claimant Sabbatai Zevi converts to Islam before the sultan.

title: The raid on the Medway
text: The Dutch sail up the Medway and burn the English fleet at its moorings.

title: Candia falls
text: Venice gives up Candia and Crete to the Ottomans after twenty-one years of siege.

title: Stenka Razin
text: The Cossack Stenka Razin leads a great revolt along the Volga before being captured and quartered in Moscow.

title: The disaster year
text: France invades the Dutch Republic; the Dutch open the dikes.

title: The De Witt brothers lynched
text: A mob in The Hague kills the Dutch leaders Johan and Cornelis de Witt and mutilates their bodies.

title: The Three Feudatories
text: Three southern generals rebel against the Kangxi emperor; the war lasts eight years.

title: Fehrbellin
text: The Great Elector of Brandenburg beats the Swedes at Fehrbellin.

title: Greenwich observatory
text: Charles II founds the Royal Observatory at Greenwich.

title: Spinoza dies
text: Spinoza dies at The Hague; his Ethics is published after his death and shocks Europe.

title: The Losiny trials
text: Witch trials in northern Moravia begin; about a hundred people burn before 1696.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Vienna plague
text: Plague kills tens of thousands in Vienna; the Plague Column on the Graben is vowed in thanks.

title: The Bohemian peasant revolt
text: Bohemian peasants rise against forced labour after plague and are put down.

title: The Affair of the Poisons
text: Fortune-tellers and poisoners at court are burned; the king's mistress is implicated.

title: Strasbourg taken
text: Louis XIV seizes the free city of Strasbourg in peacetime.

title: Versailles
text: Louis XIV moves the court to Versailles, where the nobility can be watched.

title: Peter and Ivan
text: Peter and his brother Ivan are crowned joint tsars.

title: Kahlenberg
text: Jan Sobieski breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna.

title: The Holy League
text: The emperor, Poland and Venice ally against the Ottomans.

title: The Edict of Nantes revoked
text: Louis XIV revokes the Edict of Nantes; two hundred thousand Huguenots flee France.

title: Buda retaken
text: Imperial troops take Buda back from the Ottomans after 145 years.

title: Newton's Principia
text: Newton publishes the laws of motion and gravity.

title: The Parthenon blown up
text: A Venetian shell ignites the Ottoman powder store in the Parthenon.

title: The Glorious Revolution
text: William of Orange lands in England; James II flees, and the crown passes without a war.

title: The Bill of Rights
text: The English Bill of Rights limits the crown and guarantees Parliament.

title: Nerchinsk
text: Russia and China fix their border at Nerchinsk, the first treaty between them.

title: The Boyne
text: William III beats James II at the Boyne in Ireland.

title: The Great Serb Migration
text: Tens of thousands of Serbs flee north into Habsburg Hungary as the Ottomans return.

title: The eclipse of 1691
text: An eclipse on 23 August is marked by Lasombra across Europe.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Sicilian earthquake
text: An earthquake destroys towns across eastern Sicily and kills about sixty thousand.

title: The Bank of England
text: The Bank of England is founded to lend money to the crown for war.

title: Azov taken
text: Peter the Great takes the Ottoman fortress of Azov with his new fleet.

title: Zenta
text: Prince Eugene of Savoy destroys an Ottoman army crossing the Tisza at Zenta.

title: Peter's Grand Embassy
text: Tsar Peter travels west in disguise and works in Dutch shipyards.

title: The streltsy executed
text: Peter executes over a thousand rebel musketeers and hangs bodies outside his sister's window.

title: Karlowitz
text: At Karlowitz the Ottomans give up Hungary and Transylvania; their retreat from Europe begins.

title: Narva
text: Charles XII of Sweden crushes a much larger Russian army at Narva in a snowstorm.

title: Charles II of Spain dies
text: The last Spanish Habsburg dies, leaving Spain to a French prince and Europe to war.

title: The King in Prussia
text: The Elector of Brandenburg crowns himself King in Prussia at Konigsberg.

title: The forty-seven ronin
text: Masterless samurai avenge their lord and are ordered to kill themselves.

title: St Petersburg founded
text: Peter founds a city on the Neva marshes.

title: Rakoczi's war
text: Francis II Rakoczi leads Hungary in a war of independence against the Habsburgs that lasts eight years.

title: Blenheim
text: Marlborough and Prince Eugene destroy a French and Bavarian army at Blenheim.

title: Gibraltar taken
text: An English and Dutch fleet takes Gibraltar from Spain; Britain keeps it.

title: The Acts of Union
text: The Acts of Union join England and Scotland as Great Britain.

title: Aurangzeb dies
text: Aurangzeb dies after fifty years; Mughal power begins to break apart.

title: Mount Fuji erupts
text: The last eruption of Fuji covers Edo in ash.

title: Poltava
text: Peter destroys Charles XII's army at Poltava; Russia becomes the power of the north.

title: The Great Frost
text: The coldest winter in five centuries kills crops and people.

title: Meissen porcelain
text: The first European hard porcelain is made at Meissen.

title: The Pruth
text: The Ottomans trap Peter's army on the Pruth and make the tsar give back Azov.

title: Plague in Moravia
text: Plague returns to Moravia; columns of thanks follow.

title: The Peace of Utrecht
text: The Peace of Utrecht ends the War of the Spanish Succession.

title: The Pragmatic Sanction
text: Charles VI issues the Pragmatic Sanction so his daughter can inherit the Habsburg lands.

title: George I
text: The Elector of Hanover becomes George I of Great Britain.

title: Louis XIV dies
text: Louis XIV dies after seventy-two years on the throne.

title: The Fifteen
text: A Jacobite rising in Scotland for James Stuart fails.

title: Petrovaradin
text: Prince Eugene destroys an Ottoman army at Petrovaradin.

title: Belgrade taken
text: Prince Eugene takes Belgrade from the Ottomans.

title: The Grand Lodge
text: Four London lodges of Freemasons form the first Grand Lodge.

title: The Marseille plague
text: Plague brought by a merchant ship kills half of Marseille.

title: The South Sea Bubble
text: Shares in the South Sea Company collapse and ruin thousands in Britain.

title: Peter emperor
text: Peter the Great takes the title of Emperor of All Russia.

title: Isfahan falls
text: Afghan rebels take Isfahan after a long siege and famine; the Safavid state collapses.

title: Peter dies
text: Peter the Great dies; his wife Catherine takes the throne.

title: Gulliver's Travels
text: Jonathan Swift publishes Gulliver's Travels.

title: Newton dies
text: Isaac Newton dies and is buried in Westminster Abbey.

title: Petar Blagojevich
text: An imperial official reports that a dead peasant of Kisiljevo in Serbia rose to drink the blood of his neighbours.

title: The Medvedja vampires
text: An Austrian army surgeon's report on vampires in Serbia is printed across Europe; the Masquerade strains.
ref: Real history; the World of Darkness reading is a house rule

title: The Polish Succession
text: War breaks out over the Polish throne between Russia, Austria and France.

title: Qianlong
text: The Qianlong emperor takes the Qing throne; his reign is China's last great age.

title: Nader Shah
text: Nader is crowned shah of Persia, ending the Safavid line.

title: The San Carlo
text: The San Carlo opera house of Naples opens, the oldest working opera house in Europe.

title: Nader sacks Delhi
text: Nader Shah sacks Delhi and carries off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor.

title: Belgrade returned
text: The Ottomans take back Belgrade at the peace of 1739.

title: The Silesian War
text: Frederick II of Prussia seizes Silesia from Austria; the War of the Austrian Succession begins.

title: Maria Theresa
text: Maria Theresa inherits the Habsburg lands at twenty-three and must fight to hold them.

title: The French take Prague
text: French and Bavarian troops take Prague by night; the Elector of Bavaria is crowned King of Bohemia.

title: Frederick besieges Brno
text: Prussian troops invade Moravia and besiege Brno and its Spilberk fortress, and fail.

title: The Messiah
text: Handel's Messiah is first performed in Dublin.

title: The Forty-Five
text: Charles Edward Stuart lands in Scotland and raises the clans.

title: Culloden
text: The Jacobite army is destroyed at Culloden; the Highlands are broken.

title: Calmet's treatise
text: Dom Augustin Calmet publishes his learned treatise on ghosts and vampires.

title: Aix-la-Chapelle
text: The peace of Aix-la-Chapelle leaves Silesia to Prussia.

title: Pompeii dug
text: Excavations begin at Pompeii, buried by Vesuvius in the year 79.

title: The Encyclopedie
text: Diderot and d'Alembert begin the Encyclopedie.

title: Maria Theresa against vampire hunts
text: Maria Theresa forbids the digging up and burning of corpses as vampires.

title: Lisbon
text: An earthquake, fire and sea wave destroy Lisbon.

title: The Seven Years War
text: Frederick invades Saxony and the Seven Years War begins.

title: Kolin
text: Austria beats Frederick at Kolin in Bohemia.

title: Plassey
text: The East India Company wins Bengal at Plassey.

title: Rossbach and Leuthen
text: Frederick crushes the French at Rossbach and the Austrians at Leuthen within a month.

title: Olomouc holds
text: Frederick besieges Olomouc and fails when his supply convoy is destroyed.

title: Kunersdorf
text: Russians and Austrians destroy Frederick's army at Kunersdorf.

title: George III
text: George III becomes king of Great Britain.

title: The third Panipat
text: The Afghans destroy the Maratha army at the third battle of Panipat.

title: Catherine the Great
text: Catherine takes the throne; Peter III is killed.

title: The Social Contract
text: Rousseau publishes The Social Contract: man is born free, and everywhere in chains.

title: The Peace of Paris
text: The Peace of Paris gives Britain Canada and India's trade.

title: The spinning jenny
text: Hargreaves's spinning jenny multiplies a spinner's work.

title: Buxar
text: The Company beats the Mughal emperor at Buxar and takes the revenue of Bengal.

title: Watt's engine
text: James Watt improves the steam engine with a separate condenser.

title: Russo-Turkish war
text: Catherine the Great goes to war with the Ottomans.

title: The Bengal famine
text: Famine kills perhaps ten million people in Bengal under Company rule.

title: Chesma
text: Russia burns the Ottoman fleet at Chesma.

title: The Moscow plague riot
text: Plague in Moscow kills tens of thousands and sets off a riot that kills the archbishop.

title: The first partition
text: Russia, Prussia and Austria take a third of Poland's lands.

title: Pugachev
text: A Cossack claiming to be Peter III rises.

title: The Jesuits suppressed
text: The pope dissolves the Jesuits under pressure from the Catholic kings.

title: Kuchuk Kainarji
text: At Kuchuk Kainarji Russia wins the north shore of the Black Sea.

title: Louis XVI
text: Louis XVI becomes king of France at nineteen.

title: The Bohemian peasant revolt
text: Bohemian peasants march on Prague against forced labour.

title: The Illuminati
text: Adam Weishaupt founds the Order of the Illuminati in Bavaria.

title: The Wealth of Nations
text: Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations.

title: The Potato War
text: Austria and Prussia face each other in Bohemia without fighting a battle; the soldiers dig potatoes.

title: The Gordon Riots
text: Anti-Catholic mobs burn London for a week in the Gordon Riots.

title: Joseph's patents
text: Joseph II ends personal serfdom and grants toleration to Protestants.

title: Kant's Critique
text: Kant publishes the Critique of Pure Reason.

title: Uranus
text: William Herschel finds a new planet, Uranus.

title: Balloons
text: The Montgolfier brothers fly hot-air balloons in Paris.

title: Laki
text: The Laki eruption in Iceland poisons Europe's air through a hot summer and a hard winter.

title: Russia takes the Crimea
text: Russia annexes the Crimean khanate.

title: Horea's revolt
text: Romanian peasants rise in Transylvania under Horea; Horea is broken on the wheel.

title: Figaro in Prague
text: Mozart's Marriage of Figaro is a triumph in Prague.

title: Don Giovanni
text: Mozart's Don Giovanni opens in Prague.

title: The hailstorm of 1788
text: A great hailstorm destroys France's harvests and bread prices soar.

title: The Bastille
text: Paris takes the Bastille on 14 July.

title: The Rights of Man
text: The Assembly declares the rights of man and of the citizen.

title: Joseph II dies
text: Joseph II dies, his reforms undone.

title: The flight to Varennes
text: Louis XVI is caught fleeing Paris at Varennes.

title: Mozart dies
text: Mozart dies in Vienna at thirty-five.

title: Valmy
text: The French revolutionary army holds the Prussians at Valmy.

title: The September massacres
text: Mobs kill over a thousand prisoners in the Paris jails.

title: Louis XVI guillotined
text: Louis XVI is guillotined on 21 January.

title: The Terror
text: The Committee of Public Safety's Terror kills thousands.

title: The Vendee
text: Western France rises for king and Church and is crushed with mass killings.

title: Germaine is Embraced
text: In the Revolution the Brujah Critias Embraces Germaine.
